tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__edit_version
tools.description: Publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit (some clients refuse any artifact but your own as owner-only), by replacing text in its current document: use it for a small change instead of sending the whole page to publish_version. The server reads the live index.html, applies every edit in order, and publishes the result as one new version; if any edit cannot be applied, nothing is published. Each old_text must occur exactly once in the document as it stands when that edit is applied: include enough surrounding text to make it unique. base_version must name the live version (from get_artifact, read_artifact, list_files or your last publish result); if it is no longer live the call is rejected with a conflict that names the live version: read what you are changing again and retry. To rename the artifact pass title, which also rewrites the document's <title> element; an edit to that element without title is refused, because the server keeps it in step with the artifact's title. Artifacts that contain a live (collaboratively edited) document cannot be edited here. An artifact made from a type is edited only if this server offers list_files, and only with path: one of its own text files, as list_files lists them, never its page or its type's files.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_files
tools.description: Publish an artifact from files on disk: their bytes go from the files to the artifact and do not pass through you. Prefer this to publish_version when the page's files already exist, when there is more than one file or an image, or when the page is large. For each file give `as`, the path it is served at, and `path`, its absolute path on the machine where your own file tools run; leave `uri` out. index.html is required in a new artifact. Limits for one call: 256 files, 20 MiB a file, 64 MiB in all. The client may refuse a file it will not send, such as a secrets file, a link or a path outside the working folder. Omit slug to create an artifact, private to you. To republish, give slug and base_version (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish); title and icon are kept when omitted. A republish changes only the files named and keeps the rest, which stay served: to take a file away, list it in remove. mode "replace" makes the files named the whole artifact and drops the rest. This tool publishes only to an artifact of yours. **Files Claude did not write**: Claude reads the whole file before publishing it, even when the person asks it not to. Publishing distributes the content, and Claude never distributes what it has not seen. A request for privacy is a reason to read before publishing, not an exemption. If Claude cannot read the file, it does not publish it. **Claude never publishes** a page that impersonates a real person or organization, for example by using their name, branding, byline or domain. Claude also never publishes fabricated records, receipts or reviews presented as genuine, forms or flows that collect credentials or payment details under false pretenses, or content that targets a private individual. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.

artifact_title.description: The artifact's current title, as get_artifact gives it. Needed when shared_live is 'public'.

contract.description: Optional runtime-contract version. Leave it out to keep the current one.

Required when that value is 'users' (named people or groups), 'org' (the user's whole organization) or 'public' (anyone with the link). Leave it out for a new artifact and when the value is 'owner'. slug.description: The artifact's slug. Omit to create a new artifact.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version
tools.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. Republishing is read-then-send: base_version must name the live version you are replacing (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result) — if it is no longer live, the publish is rejected with a conflict; re-read and retry from the current state. On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB.

schema.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version
schema.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. Republishing is read-then-send: base_version must name the live version you are replacing (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result) — if it is no longer live, the publish is rejected with a conflict; re-read and retry from the current state. On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB.

artifact_title.description: The artifact's current title, as get_artifact gives it. Needed when shared_live is 'public'.

base_version.description: Required when slug is given: the version id this publish replaces — echo the version get_artifact or read_artifact returned (or your last publish result's). Rejected with a conflict if it no longer names the live version, so concurrent edits are never silently overwritten. Omit when creating.

content.description: The complete HTML document, at most 16 MiB. Must sniff as text/html — begin it with <!DOCTYPE html>.

contract.description: Optional runtime-contract version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Leave it out to keep the current one. Pass one only when the user asks for a different version, or this server's answer says to. If the publish is rejected because the contract is yanked or out of the supported window, republish with an explicit "0.0.0" to clear the contract — omitting the argument is not a reliable recovery (the server may carry the stored contract forward, repeating the rejection).

deadline.description: Optional, rarely needed: by when pages still open on an OLDER version must have moved to this one — one word: now, 15m, 1h, 24h, 7d, or an ISO-8601 time at most 30 days ahead. Omit it for ordinary edits (open pages then move at their next quiet moment); it cannot be relaxed once published.

favicon.description: Optional legacy emoji marker; omit it.

icon.description: One short, generic word for the artifact's tab icon — a plain signifier of what it is, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map; not a product or brand name. Pass one when creating; omit when republishing to keep the current icon.

shared_live.description: States who the artifact you are republishing is already shared with, and changes nothing: its 'read' value from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result. Required when that value is 'users' (named people or groups), 'org' (the user's whole organization) or 'public' (anyone with the link). Leave it out for a new artifact and when the value is 'owner'. Rejected if it does not match the artifact's current value.

slug.description: The artifact's server-assigned slug (UUID), e.g. from list_artifacts, get_artifact or the artifact's own URL. Omit to create a new artifact.

title.description: Browser-tab title. Required when creating. When republishing it is optional — omitted, the new version keeps the current live version's title (the server also keeps the stored HTML's <title> element in sync with it); pass a value only to rename the artifact, never invent a new title on a routine republish.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__read_artifact
tools.description: Read the current document of an artifact: one that the user owns, or one that belongs to someone in the user's organization and that the user can open. Read a pasted claude.ai artifact link with this tool. Returns a JSON summary (slug, version id, title, favicon, runtime-contract version, total_lines, and for a multi-file artifact its file names), then the HTML of the version the user is served, then a reminder. The HTML, and the summary's title, favicon and file names, are wrapped in an <untrusted-document-...> tag that the summary's notice names; the tag is not part of them. A document over ~1 MiB is not served whole: read it in parts with offset and limit, which count lines; next_offset says where the next part starts. ## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

| Tool | Credits |
|------|---------|

| meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d | table below |
| meshy_text_to_3d_refine / meshy_retexture | 10 (15 with texture_resolution "8k") |
| meshy_remesh / meshy_rig (incl. walking + running) / meshy_uv_unwrap | 5 |
| meshy_animate | 3 per action |
| meshy_text_to_motion | 10 (prime) / 3 (swift) |
| meshy_repair_printability / meshy_process_multicolor / meshy_auto_split | 10 |
| meshy_convert / meshy_resize | 1 |
| meshy_creative_lab | 36; keycap 62; fidget-collapsible 6 |

| analyze printability, balance, usage, animation library, status, list, download | free |

| image / multi-image ai_model | mesh only | + 2K/4K texture | + 8K texture |
|---|---|---|---|

If a create call fails with a timeout, network error or 5xx, the task may still have been created and charged. Check meshy_list_tasks (task_type = that task's type) for it before calling the create tool again. A wait that times out leaves the task running: poll the same task_id again.

target_formats is fixed at creation time (3mf only when listed), so ask about the intended use first.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL. When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in this conversation or in a local file. Claude publishes it and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. No user-decision item remains open in this file.
16	
17	## Summary
18	
19	In-World Instruments & Inspect View draws every reading the ship itself produces (wall and panel dials, tank sight-glasses, state glyphs, housing glow marks and a module's own state frames) as lit sprites that can be read only where the player's chest beam, a fixture or a thrown glowstick reaches them, plus a precise, verdict-free inspect card for one lit instrument at a time. It asks the Perception Filter for the value the local player is shown and draws it with three honest or dishonest motions (a step, then rest for a real change and a heavier damped settle for a real jump; a tremor under real stress; a never-resting glide for a lie), carrying the lie's violet edge and nothing else; it simulates, persists and decides nothing. Read it if you are building anything that draws a gauge or the card, authoring instrument content or a lie target, or checking that no schematic, status screen or condition word has crept into the game.
20	
21	> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Presentation` · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `Life-Support Graph (designed)`, `2D Lighting & Occlusion (designed in this run)`, `Perception Filter (designed in this run)`, `Interaction System (designed in this run)`, `Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query (designed)`, `Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera (designed)`, `Player Controller & Input (designed; reply owed)`, `HUD & Suit Layer (designed in this run)`, `Debug Overlay (designed in this run)`, `Accessibility Settings (undesigned)`
22	
23	## Overview
24	
25	**What it is, in one sentence.** In-World Instruments & Inspect View is the presentation system that draws every reading the ship itself produces — dials, tank sight-glasses, state glyphs, housing glow marks and a module's own state frames — as lit sprites on the walls and machines of the world (layer 0), and draws the same instrument again at HUD size as the inspect card (layer 2) when the player stands in its light and asks for a precise reading.
26	
27	**The data layer.** It simulates nothing and persists nothing. Each frame, for each instrument on screen, it asks the Perception Filter for the value the local player is shown (`perceived(ref, viewer)`, PF-7), maps the returned per-mille reading to a needle angle, a meniscus row or a digit string through a per-instrument calibration record (the answer to PF-45), and draws it with one of the three motion signatures of art bible 7.3: **settle** (a damped step for an honest jump, drawn on the bus-load dial only at MVP, D.4) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, **tremor** (an irregular shake around a true value while the ship is really under stress) or **glide** (the Filter's uncaused, never-resting drift of a lie). It reads the Life-Support Graph's `read_view` only for non-value inputs (which honest frame a module shows, whether the bound subject is under physical stress, whether an alarm is eligible, whether the binding still exists), never calls `true_value`, and never decides whether, when, for whom or by how much anything lies: that is the Filter's and Sanity's. It registers **zero** sim blocks, hooks, mutators, commands or persisted fields; it is a `PRESENTATION` subscriber (KRN:106-110; PIPE PR-8).
28	
29	**The player-facing effect.** The player meets it as the ship's own voice, read by their own light. A gauge on a wall is readable exactly as far as the beam, a fixture, a lantern pool or a Chemlight glowstick reaches it ("What You Light, You Can Read"); the needle sits in a zone band coded by pattern as well as hue, with no numerals at game-camera distance; the player reads cause, mass and rest at a glance (a needle that steps to a new reading and comes to rest, and eases heavily when the change is a real jump; a needle that shakes under real stress) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* and learns the one motion that has no cause, no mass and no rest: the lie. When precision matters they stand still in their own light and press `inspect`: a card appears beside the instrument carrying its label, the same needle and zone band, and one numeral with its unit — never a state word or a verdict. The card is the same instrument, not a second one: it lies exactly when its wall gauge lies (advisor ruling R13), so inspecting is a precision tool and never a free falsifier. The real check is always a different reading elsewhere or the consequence channel the Graph and Failure & Trail draw (frost, drip, draught, hiss, breath, a rotor's sound).
30	
31	**What the game loses without it.** The core hypothesis — a tense 30-plus-minute solo session over a visible life-support graph — has no surface on which the graph can be read or lied through. The MVP hallucination is class (b) only (CON "MVP Definition" item 5; SN-16), and class (b) lives on exactly the surfaces owned here (gauge needle, the card's numeral as a mode of the needle's lie, state glyph, lamp-housing glow frame, machine state frame, inspect card; PF-5 row 20). Without it the falsification economy cannot run, the Graph's third diegetic surface (LSG:996-1003) does not exist, and the gamepad has no HR-14 mirror card.
32	
33	**Scope — "module-body reading surfaces" (advisor ruling R7, R24).** This GDD owns (a) every gauge, dial, level sight-glass and state glyph produced by the ship or a derelict, (b) the inspect card, and (c) the bounded **Module-Body Presenter**: the *selection* among a module sheet's honest state frames (running/stopped, whole/cracked, lamp lit/unlit, WORN wear) and the drawing of the state glyph. It owns no module art (Item DB `sprite_family`), no placement (Layout and Derelict Authoring), no module behaviour, and nothing suit-produced or hand-held (Suit & Equipment and HUD & Suit Layer own those, including the field-check reading, advisor ruling R15). It draws **no schematic, overlay, minimap, ship-status or loop-summary screen, ever** (advisor ruling R16; LSG:51 anti-pillar 3: "Precision exists only as the lit inspect card of a specific instrument").
34	
35	**MVP scope.** MVP-live: DIAL_L, DIAL_S and the LINEAR tank sight-glass with honest settle, tremor and the stress notch; the inspect card (label, dial, numeral); the gleam on wall and card; the in-world alarm mark on DIAL_L, panel and tank housings; honest WORN wear and the DEAD frame; the stage-2 state glyph and housing pip; the stage-3 machine-frame selection for lie-capable modules (SN-16 reach); the 18-instrument indicative manifest on the LSG slice (home 9, A 4, B 5 for a seat with a usable scanner; the per-site range with and without one is in IW-29) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; BLOCKING 1)*; single seat. Later: co-op seat behaviour (E-IW-57, E-IW-58, AC-IW-85 exercised at the co-op tier), `strain` dials (OQ-IW-5), conditional `CARD_MAG` 2 (OQ-IW-15), powered gauges (OQ-IW-11), card navigation, the channelled INSPECT verb (VS-A), and the Accessibility Settings screen-reader text (Alpha).
36	
37	**Index wording, reconciled.** IDX:39 says: "Owns the gauge, sight-glass and dial nodes as lit sprites and the inspect view (the same instrument magnified); asks the Perception Filter for the displayed value and draws it with the settle/tremor/glide motion signatures. *Why this tier:* Where class (b) lies live; pairs with the Failure & Trail System as the truth check." Reconciled with the rulings: "sight-glass" means the fill-level reading of a tank (the flow pattern and moving medium on pipes are world-state witnesses drawn by Lighting and Failure & Trail, advisor ruling R8); "the same instrument magnified" means the same ref, the same drawn value and the same leak, shown at HUD scale `H` with a label and a numeral (advisor ruling R2, R13); "pairs with Failure & Trail as the truth check" means the two never share a node (FT:314). The index's dependency list (Life-Support Graph, 2D Lighting & Occlusion, Perception Filter, Interaction System) is accurate but incomplete; the missing edges are listed in Dependencies and flagged, not edited (advisor ruling R26).
38	
39	**Dependency status at authoring (Glob of `design/gdd/`, 2026-10-27).** Life-Support Graph — designed (locked). 2D Lighting & Occlusion, Perception Filter, Interaction System — designed in this run. Player Controller & Input, Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera, Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query, Sanity & Hallucination Rules, Item & Module Database, Failure & Trail, Derelict Authoring, Ship Section & Layout, Boarding & Salvage, Web Map & Transit, Suit & Equipment, Adaptive Audio & Tells, Attention, Horror — on disk and read where they name this system. Chart Table & Menus — designed (boundary only). **HUD & Suit Layer and Debug Overlay (True Values) — designed in this run** (header Status Designed; re-read 2026-10-27 for HS-3, HS-14, HS-33, HS-47, HS-52, HS-56, HS-57, DO-12, DO-22: they agree with IW-14, IW-22, IW-23, IW-35 and IW-38 apart from the HS-52 cursor, OQ-IW-21, and the HUD-owned counting unit, OQ-IW-9). Accessibility Settings — **has no file** (`(provisional — Accessibility Settings undesigned)`). No ADRs and no `design/ux/instruments.md` exist yet (LSG:1003 asks for the latter before epics).
40	
41	## Player Fantasy
42	
43	### Framing (direct, per Category UI)
44	
45	**You read a dying ship by its own needles, in your own light, and you learn which needles to trust.** The player is not a captain at a status board; there is no board. They are the person who walks up to a wall in the dark, lets the chest lamp fall across a scratched bezel, watches a needle step to its new reading and come to rest, and knows from angle and zone alone that the reservoir is low. When precision matters they stand still in their own light and bring the instrument close. And at some point the needle starts to slide with nothing in the ship to explain it, a thin violet edge sits on the glass, and the player has to decide whether to believe the ship or the gauge. The answer the game teaches is always the same: **believe the ship** (P1). This system is where that sentence becomes something the player holds.
46	
47	*Framing choice (logged).* Three candidate framings were weighed: (a) **direct — "the ship's own voice, read by your light"**, (b) the mechanic's glance (fluency), (c) the doubting reader (epistemics). (a) is chosen because it is the only framing whose design pressure points the same way as every locked guard rail (LSG:51 no schematic, ART 3.1 no numerals at distance, EM-22 no dwell, PF-4 default truth, the card-is-the-gauge rule). (b) and (c) are real feelings that appear *as the session arc* — (b) mid-session, as reading becomes fluent, (c) late and deep, as the glance stops being enough — but neither is a design driver: (b) would push toward numerals on world gauges and a status glance (P3 and P1 strain), (c) toward a lie detector and a "lies caught" score (P1 and P5 strain). Fantasy-as-role ("be a starship engineer") is deliberately not first: it would push toward more instruments and a console to sit at. The fantasy is the act of *reading under doubt*, which needs few instruments, each one meaningful.
48	
49	**MDA rank, local to this system.** (1) Discovery: finding out what the ship is doing, and whether the reading is lying. (2) Challenge delivered as Competence: reading cause, mass and rest at a glance and choosing the cheapest truth check. (3) Fellowship *(co-op tier; the MVP is single-seat, so solo the cross-check is a second dial, the scanner or the witness, *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*)*: the cross-check. P4's "Crewmates Are Instruments" lives here: a teammate's body is the honest second reading ("you're fogging up"), a teammate's beam keeping my gauge lit (IW-25) is a shared act of reading, and, in co-op, the cheapest truth check is often a question asked across a room. (4) Sensation: the settle, the tremor, the tick of a digit, the gleam on glass — instruments are the most tactile UI in the game, but Sensation is deliberately ranked fourth so the presentation layer never drifts toward the "juicy UI" that ART 7.3 rejected. **SDT:** Autonomy — the player chooses where to spend light, whether to inspect, which truth check to pay for; Competence — the motion grammar is learnable and consistent; Relatedness — in co-op the other player's body is the honest cross-check ("you look cold" costs only light, ART:738), and no instrument ever reads a crewmate: the crewmate is the instrument.
50	
51	### Pillar lines this system embodies (verbatim)
52

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

17	## Summary
18	
19	In-World Instruments & Inspect View draws every reading the ship itself produces (wall and panel dials, tank sight-glasses, state glyphs, housing glow marks and a module's own state frames) as lit sprites that can be read only where the player's chest beam, a fixture or a thrown glowstick reaches them, plus a precise, verdict-free inspect card for one lit instrument at a time. It asks the Perception Filter for the value the local player is shown and draws it with three honest or dishonest motions (a step, then rest for a real change and a heavier damped settle for a real jump; a tremor under real stress; a never-resting glide for a lie), carrying the lie's violet edge and nothing else; it simulates, persists and decides nothing. Read it if you are building anything that draws a gauge or the card, authoring instrument content or a lie target, or checking that no schematic, status screen or condition word has crept into the game.
20	
21	> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Presentation` · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `Life-Support Graph (designed)`, `2D Lighting & Occlusion (designed in this run)`, `Perception Filter (designed in this run)`, `Interaction System (designed in this run)`, `Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query (designed)`, `Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera (designed)`, `Player Controller & Input (designed; reply owed)`, `HUD & Suit Layer (designed in this run)`, `Debug Overlay (designed in this run)`, `Accessibility Settings (undesigned)`
22	
23	## Overview
24	
25	**What it is, in one sentence.** In-World Instruments & Inspect View is the presentation system that draws every reading the ship itself produces — dials, tank sight-glasses, state glyphs, housing glow marks and a module's own state frames — as lit sprites on the walls and machines of the world (layer 0), and draws the same instrument again at HUD size as the inspect card (layer 2) when the player stands in its light and asks for a precise reading.
26	
27	**The data layer.** It simulates nothing and persists nothing. Each frame, for each instrument on screen, it asks the Perception Filter for the value the local player is shown (`perceived(ref, viewer)`, PF-7), maps the returned per-mille reading to a needle angle, a meniscus row or a digit string through a per-instrument calibration record (the answer to PF-45), and draws it with one of the three motion signatures of art bible 7.3: **settle** (a damped step for an honest jump, drawn on the bus-load dial only at MVP, D.4) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, **tremor** (an irregular shake around a true value while the ship is really under stress) or **glide** (the Filter's uncaused, never-resting drift of a lie). It reads the Life-Support Graph's `read_view` only for non-value inputs (which honest frame a module shows, whether the bound subject is under physical stress, whether an alarm is eligible, whether the binding still exists), never calls `true_value`, and never decides whether, when, for whom or by how much anything lies: that is the Filter's and Sanity's. It registers **zero** sim blocks, hooks, mutators, commands or persisted fields; it is a `PRESENTATION` subscriber (KRN:106-110; PIPE PR-8).
28	
29	**The player-facing effect.** The player meets it as the ship's own voice, read by their own light. A gauge on a wall is readable exactly as far as the beam, a fixture, a lantern pool or a Chemlight glowstick reaches it ("What You Light, You Can Read"); the needle sits in a zone band coded by pattern as well as hue, with no numerals at game-camera distance; the player reads cause, mass and rest at a glance (a needle that steps to a new reading and comes to rest, and eases heavily when the change is a real jump; a needle that shakes under real stress) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* and learns the one motion that has no cause, no mass and no rest: the lie. When precision matters they stand still in their own light and press `inspect`: a card appears beside the instrument carrying its label, the same needle and zone band, and one numeral with its unit — never a state word or a verdict. The card is the same instrument, not a second one: it lies exactly when its wall gauge lies (advisor ruling R13), so inspecting is a precision tool and never a free falsifier. The real check is always a different reading elsewhere or the consequence channel the Graph and Failure & Trail draw (frost, drip, draught, hiss, breath, a rotor's sound).
30	
31	**What the game loses without it.** The core hypothesis — a tense 30-plus-minute solo session over a visible life-support graph — has no surface on which the graph can be read or lied through. The MVP hallucination is class (b) only (CON "MVP Definition" item 5; SN-16), and class (b) lives on exactly the surfaces owned here (gauge needle, the card's numeral as a mode of the needle's lie, state glyph, lamp-housing glow frame, machine state frame, inspect card; PF-5 row 20). Without it the falsification economy cannot run, the Graph's third diegetic surface (LSG:996-1003) does not exist, and the gamepad has no HR-14 mirror card.
32	
33	**Scope — "module-body reading surfaces" (advisor ruling R7, R24).** This GDD owns (a) every gauge, dial, level sight-glass and state glyph produced by the ship or a derelict, (b) the inspect card, and (c) the bounded **Module-Body Presenter**: the *selection* among a module sheet's honest state frames (running/stopped, whole/cracked, lamp lit/unlit, WORN wear) and the drawing of the state glyph. It owns no module art (Item DB `sprite_family`), no placement (Layout and Derelict Authoring), no module behaviour, and nothing suit-produced or hand-held (Suit & Equipment and HUD & Suit Layer own those, including the field-check reading, advisor ruling R15). It draws **no schematic, overlay, minimap, ship-status or loop-summary screen, ever** (advisor ruling R16; LSG:51 anti-pillar 3: "Precision exists only as the lit inspect card of a specific instrument").
34	
35	**MVP scope.** MVP-live: DIAL_L, DIAL_S and the LINEAR tank sight-glass with honest settle, tremor and the stress notch; the inspect card (label, dial, numeral); the gleam on wall and card; the in-world alarm mark on DIAL_L, panel and tank housings; honest WORN wear and the DEAD frame; the stage-2 state glyph and housing pip; the stage-3 machine-frame selection for lie-capable modules (SN-16 reach); the 18-instrument indicative manifest on the LSG slice (home 9, A 4, B 5 for a seat with a usable scanner; the per-site range with and without one is in IW-29) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; BLOCKING 1)*; single seat. Later: co-op seat behaviour (E-IW-57, E-IW-58, AC-IW-85 exercised at the co-op tier), `strain` dials (OQ-IW-5), conditional `CARD_MAG` 2 (OQ-IW-15), powered gauges (OQ-IW-11), card navigation, the channelled INSPECT verb (VS-A), and the Accessibility Settings screen-reader text (Alpha).
36	
37	**Index wording, reconciled.** IDX:39 says: "Owns the gauge, sight-glass and dial nodes as lit sprites and the inspect view (the same instrument magnified); asks the Perception Filter for the displayed value and draws it with the settle/tremor/glide motion signatures. *Why this tier:* Where class (b) lies live; pairs with the Failure & Trail System as the truth check." Reconciled with the rulings: "sight-glass" means the fill-level reading of a tank (the flow pattern and moving medium on pipes are world-state witnesses drawn by Lighting and Failure & Trail, advisor ruling R8); "the same instrument magnified" means the same ref, the same drawn value and the same leak, shown at HUD scale `H` with a label and a numeral (advisor ruling R2, R13); "pairs with Failure & Trail as the truth check" means the two never share a node (FT:314). The index's dependency list (Life-Support Graph, 2D Lighting & Occlusion, Perception Filter, Interaction System) is accurate but incomplete; the missing edges are listed in Dependencies and flagged, not edited (advisor ruling R26).
38	
39	**Dependency status at authoring (Glob of `design/gdd/`, 2026-10-27).** Life-Support Graph — designed (locked). 2D Lighting & Occlusion, Perception Filter, Interaction System — designed in this run. Player Controller & Input, Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera, Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query, Sanity & Hallucination Rules, Item & Module Database, Failure & Trail, Derelict Authoring, Ship Section & Layout, Boarding & Salvage, Web Map & Transit, Suit & Equipment, Adaptive Audio & Tells, Attention, Horror — on disk and read where they name this system. Chart Table & Menus — designed (boundary only). **HUD & Suit Layer and Debug Overlay (True Values) — designed in this run** (header Status Designed; re-read 2026-10-27 for HS-3, HS-14, HS-33, HS-47, HS-52, HS-56, HS-57, DO-12, DO-22: they agree with IW-14, IW-22, IW-23, IW-35 and IW-38 apart from the HS-52 cursor, OQ-IW-21, and the HUD-owned counting unit, OQ-IW-9). Accessibility Settings — **has no file** (`(provisional — Accessibility Settings undesigned)`). No ADRs and no `design/ux/instruments.md` exist yet (LSG:1003 asks for the latter before epics).
40	
41	## Player Fantasy
42	
43	### Framing (direct, per Category UI)
44	
45	**You read a dying ship by its own needles, in your own light, and you learn which needles to trust.** The player is not a captain at a status board; there is no board. They are the person who walks up to a wall in the dark, lets the chest lamp fall across a scratched bezel, watches a needle step to its new reading and come to rest, and knows from angle and zone alone that the reservoir is low. When precision matters they stand still in their own light and bring the instrument close. And at some point the needle starts to slide with nothing in the ship to explain it, a thin violet edge sits on the glass, and the player has to decide whether to believe the ship or the gauge. The answer the game teaches is always the same: **believe the ship** (P1). This system is where that sentence becomes something the player holds.
46	
47	*Framing choice (logged).* Three candidate framings were weighed: (a) **direct — "the ship's own voice, read by your light"**, (b) the mechanic's glance (fluency), (c) the doubting reader (epistemics). (a) is chosen because it is the only framing whose design pressure points the same way as every locked guard rail (LSG:51 no schematic, ART 3.1 no numerals at distance, EM-22 no dwell, PF-4 default truth, the card-is-the-gauge rule). (b) and (c) are real feelings that appear *as the session arc* — (b) mid-session, as reading becomes fluent, (c) late and deep, as the glance stops being enough — but neither is a design driver: (b) would push toward numerals on world gauges and a status glance (P3 and P1 strain), (c) toward a lie detector and a "lies caught" score (P1 and P5 strain). Fantasy-as-role ("be a starship engineer") is deliberately not first: it would push toward more instruments and a console to sit at. The fantasy is the act of *reading under doubt*, which needs few instruments, each one meaningful.
48	
49	**MDA rank, local to this system.** (1) Discovery: finding out what the ship is doing, and whether the reading is lying. (2) Challenge delivered as Competence: reading cause, mass and rest at a glance and choosing the cheapest truth check. (3) Fellowship *(co-op tier; the MVP is single-seat, so solo the cross-check is a second dial, the scanner or the witness, *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*)*: the cross-check. P4's "Crewmates Are Instruments" lives here: a teammate's body is the honest second reading ("you're fogging up"), a teammate's beam keeping my gauge lit (IW-25) is a shared act of reading, and, in co-op, the cheapest truth check is often a question asked across a room. (4) Sensation: the settle, the tremor, the tick of a digit, the gleam on glass — instruments are the most tactile UI in the game, but Sensation is deliberately ranked fourth so the presentation layer never drifts toward the "juicy UI" that ART 7.3 rejected. **SDT:** Autonomy — the player chooses where to spend light, whether to inspect, which truth check to pay for; Competence — the motion grammar is learnable and consistent; Relatedness — in co-op the other player's body is the honest cross-check ("you look cold" costs only light, ART:738), and no instrument ever reads a crewmate: the crewmate is the instrument.
50	
51	### Pillar lines this system embodies (verbatim)
52	
53	| Pillar | Verbatim line | What the player physically does |
54	|---|---|---|
55	| P1 The World Never Lies | "Only instruments and perception can be wrong." Design test: "a hidden stat vs. a visibly leaking pipe -> the pipe" | reads a gauge, then confirms it against frost, drip, breath, draught or a rotor's sound; the instrument is the one thing allowed to be wrong |
56	| P4 Sanity Rewrites Reality | "(b) False system states. Broken reads as fixed, fixed as broken; the lie extends from the gauge to the sprite." / "No lie is unfalsifiable ... checking costs time, risk or trust." Secondary test: "-10% move speed vs. a gauge showing a false value -> the false gauge" | catches a reading that glides, falsifies it by walking to the thing the gauge is about, by a second instrument or by a crewmate |
57	| P3 The Web Watches (Visual Identity Anchor) | "What You Light, You Can Read." "Light is a resource you spend; inside your light, every pipe is a sentence; outside it, the dark is honest." | spends light and stillness to read; a dark gauge is unreadable, never "unknown" |
58	| P2 Dread Before Chaos (serves) | "Every breach is preceded by a tell" | sees an honest needle shake under real stress; the shake is the instrument's share of the tell |
59	
60	Art bible 7.3 already wrote the lesson in one line and it is quoted here as the player-facing test: **"A player who learns 'needles that wander are lying; needles that shake are warning' has learned Pillar 2 and Pillar 4 from the same gauge."**

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

</system-reminder>

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

</system-reminder>

61	
62	### Design tests (this system's own, pillar format)
63	
64	> *A reading the player can trust by looking at the screen vs. a reading the player must spend light, stillness or a walk to trust -> the second.*
65	
66	1. **Card vs gauge.** A card more trustworthy than its wall gauge vs. a card that is exactly the gauge, magnified -> exactly the gauge (R1, R13; ART:747; SN-16 AD-C1).
67	2. **Cause of a doubt.** A UI element that tells the player a reading is lying vs. a world the player can walk to that disagrees with the reading -> the world. Any feature that signals a lie without a world cause or the HR-5 leak (a "suspect" icon, a confidence colour, a stability readout) fails (P1; PF-38).
68	3. **Motion grammar.** A needle that moves for a reason the player cannot find vs. a needle whose every honest motion has a cause, has mass and rests -> the second; and the one motion with no cause, no mass and no rest is the lie (ART 7.3).
69	4. **Precision vs exposure.** Precision at a distance vs. precision that needs the instrument inside your own light -> the second (P3; R4, R20). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* Under the ratified rules the card itself is free to open and to close (D94, no Attention stimulus, IW-24), so the cost belongs to reading, not to the card: the player must stand with the gauge lit, in a dark room, for as long as they read. Opening the card is harmless to spam because of card parity (it is never a falsifier, IW-26); the exposure the player feels comes from the dark room and from standing lit.
70	
71	### Anchor moments (one ladder, three beats)
72	
73	Ids are real MVP ids from Derelict Authoring and the Graph slice; times are illustrative; every number quoted is an owner value.
74	
75	**Beat A, the anchor: the honest read in the dark (minute 2 of a fresh wake, sanity stage 0).** `cryo_bay` is in the FROST band (authored T -2000 mC, DA:197; LS-7 FROST is -15000..-1 mC, LSG:76); the ship is dark except the player's chest beam.
76	
77	| t (s) | What happens | Rule it shows |
78	|---|---|---|
79	| 0.0 | The player turns; the chest beam (from the per-facing chest point, PC) slides across the north wall. A dial housing is visible as geometry; its face is unreadable. | P3: the dark is honest, not hidden; the housing is physical (ART 7.0) |
80	| 0.3 | The beam crosses `LIT_ON_PM` 150 on the gauge (EM-22). The face is readable; the prompt plate shows the keybind and a state-neutral verb. | What You Light, You Can Read |
81	| 0.3-0.6 | The needle is simply where the reading is. No settle on becoming lit: a settle is an honest *change*, not a reveal. | ART 7.3; IW-12 |
82	| 1.0 | The needle sits in the cold zone (a hatched band, readable without hue). The player looks down: frost on the pod rims, the drip trail (consequence channel). Reading and witness agree; the needle does not tremble: a cold band is a state, not a stress. | P1 design test: the pipe |
83	| 2.0 | The player presses `inspect`. The card opens beside the gauge: a label, the same needle and zones, one numeral with its unit. No word such as "cold" or "FROST". | precision needs the gauge in the beam *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
84	| 2.0-6.0 | Movement intent is zeroed on entry and the first step past the dead-zone closes the card and moves in the same frame (IW-25); the sim keeps ticking. The player stands still, lit, in a dark room. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | P3: reading spends light and restraint |
85	| 6.0 | The player turns away. The light leaves the gauge, `lit` falls below `LIT_OFF_PM` 120 and the card closes at once; the face goes dark. | EM-22: no dwell |
86	
87	*What the player should feel:* competent and careful. Any exposure they feel comes from the dark room and from standing lit while they read, not from the card, which costs nothing to open or close *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. They learned three things without a tutorial line: light makes it readable; the reading agrees with the frost; reading precisely means keeping the gauge in the beam.
88	
89	**Beat B: the first lie (stage 1, `engine_room`, the home loop running fault-free).** The first lie in any world is FALSE_FAIL or GLIDE on a fault-free lit subject with all three leak modes (SN-16). The oxygen-partial-pressure dial `inst_engine_room_p_o2` reads NORMAL; the home loop is running, fault-free. About ten seconds after the player enters, the needle begins to slide toward the alarm side with nothing in the room to explain it, never resting (at an 18 art px needle the Filter's `rate_floor` is 1.59 deg/s, PF-17, so about 16 degrees in 10 s); a thin violet fringe (`#B07BE6`, never the core `#8A3FD1`) sits on the glass edge; a faint wrong-pitched tick sounds (`FA_LIE_SIG_GAUGE`, PF-20). Each mode alone is sufficient (HR-5). The player opens the card and **the card glides too**, with the same gleam: precision did not save them (R13). They check the cheapest truth: their own breath, the room's witness, a second reading (`suit.o2` for the room they stand in, which counts because the first lie is ALARM-direction, or another compartment's gauge, SN-15 L-2I) or a `field_check` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; BLOCKING 1)*. The lie returns to truth on the glide path, unannounced, identically whether it expired or was debunked; the game never says "that was a hallucination". *Feeling:* a cold prickle, then the satisfaction of catching it with the world. P4 test: "a hallucination that can never be disproved vs. one that costs time, risk or trust to disprove -> the costly one."
90	
91	**Beat C: the lie that can kill (stage 2 or later, a remote reading).** L-G forbids a FALSE_OK on the quantity of the compartment the seat stands in while that band is outside OK (SN-15 L-G; the earlier SN:260 line cite is stale *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), and L-S keeps lethal faults out of any comfort-direction lie (not only FALSE_OK) below `LETHAL_FAULT_MIN_STAGE` 2 (SN-15 L-S and Sanity's Tuning Knobs table; the earlier SN:1054 cite is stale), so the lethal lie is always a **remote** reading. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Worked fixtures** (proposed placements; the hop counts are verified against the Derelict Authoring room trees, DA C.2 and C.3; placement itself stays Derelict Authoring's and Layout's). **Derelict B.** `inst_b_dock_p_o2`, a DIAL_L on the `b_spine` wall beside `door_b_dock_spine` (`mount_room` `b_spine`), reads the `p_o2` of `b_dock` (`subject_room`): `hops` = 1 (tree `b_dock - b_spine`), inside `WITNESS_HOPS_MAX` 2. After the weld the O2-ROOM seam leak at the `airlock` / `b_dock` seam is on the `lethal_fault_modes` list (Sanity SN-15 L-S) and the gauge shows NORMAL (FALSE_OK). **Derelict A.** `inst_a_machine_T`, a DIAL_L in `a_spine` beside the CLOSED `door_a_spine_machine`, reads the `T` of `a_machine` (-22000 mC, the one lethal-cold room, DA-28): `hops` = 1 (tree `a_dock - a_spine - {a_life, a_machine}`), and its witness is the frost fan reaching the door sill. That lie is a cold-band lie and not a `lethal_fault_modes` fault; whether Sanity gates it as lethal is OQ-IW-35. Both gauges are the Beat C fixtures of AC-IW-109. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; BLOCKING 1)* Both are REMOTE and take a COMFORT-direction lie, for which the suit is never a second reading (SN-15 L-2I) and a REMOTE row gets no suit credit at all, so each fixture is **scanner-dependent**: the lie is drawn only for a seat that carries `tool_scanner` and is not hauling a module (SE-11: `equip_tool` is `BUSY` while carrying). A seat that walks toward the gauge with a module in hand is not lied to on it. A fixed second `p_o2` dial in `b_spine` would make fixture B seat-independent (the IW-29 ask); fixture A stays scanner-dependent (OQ-IW-35). The home ship has no lethal-class remote fixture in this manifest: `inst_cryo_bay_p_o2` hangs in the room it reads and so cannot produce Beat C. A witness is active in the fault's compartment within `WITNESS_HOPS_MAX` 2 (Sanity-owned, L-W): a hiss at the seam, a draught at the door, the strain sound. The player who trusts the gauge walks in without topping up and the room is DECOMP; the body counts honestly. Per the binding user decision ("death is a bitch. It happens."), a player who ignores the hiss can die, and at MVP restarts from the last autosave (Save/Load). The player who listens at the door, walks to the witness, scans the gauge or reads a second fixed dial lives; in the co-op tier a crewmate inside ("you're fogging up") is one more honest reading *(co-op tier)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **That is the whole fantasy in one moment: the gauge said fine, and it was leaking; the ship said otherwise; the ship was right.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* The comfort lie wears the same HR-5 tell the player has already learned (the never-resting needle, the violet fringe, the wrong-pitched tick, SN L-L), so the gauge's own leak is something the player could have caught: the death reads as "I ignored the leak and the hiss", not "the game cheated" (the Beat C attribution criterion below). The lethal remote lie is never contradicted by a mark on its own housing: the alarm mark (IW-19) is drawn only where the alarm-eligible subject physically is, and a gauge whose subject is in another compartment (`hops` >= 1, the derived REMOTE flag of IW-8) never carries it, so the FALSE_OK needle in a normal zone has no lit Alarm Red beside it to falsify it by glance. Falsifying it still costs a walk, a second reading or, in the co-op tier, a crewmate (P4). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*

93	### How the fantasy deepens, not breaks, under hallucination
94	
95	The rule that keeps the ladder fair is ART 7.3's: **"The mechanism is always honest; only the value lies."** The needle still pivots, the digit still ticks in steps, the housing is still geometry, the alarm mark still means the real alarm. The lie is only ever *where the needle points* (or which honest frame is shown); the player never has to doubt the physics of an instrument, only its testimony.
96	
97	| Sanity stage (SN-16 reach; `LIES_MAX` 1/2/4) | Surfaces that may lie (drawn here) | What the player learns |
98	|---|---|---|
99	| 0 | none | Read cause, mass and rest; match every reading to a witness. Tremor is a real warning (P2). |
100	| 1 | gauge needle, and the card (its needle and its numeral are the same ref's `Perceived`; the numeral is a card-visible mode of the needle's lie, not a second surface) | "Wandering needles lie; shaking needles warn." Precision (the card) is not proof. The first lie is cheap and fault-free, so the lesson lands without punishment. |
101	| 2 | + state glyph, + lamp-housing glow frame (including the housing pip, R21) | Finding a gauge by its glow is not proof its loop runs. Remote readings can now hide lethal faults (Beat C). |
102	| 3 | + whole machine sprite state frames (SPRITE_SWAP, both honest frames required) | "The lie extends from the gauge to the sprite." A rotor may spin on a stopped machine; only the consequence channel and other people remain. |
103	
104	**What must survive every stage (the fantasy's floor).** At least one channel of truth (P4): the consequence channel (LSG:168) is never drawn or corrupted by this GDD, and L-2I keeps one honest second reading per loop per seat (SN-15 L-2I; the suit counts only against an ALARM-direction lie). The HR-5 leak on every lie (gleam and motion mode mandatory, only SOUND droppable, PF-8; never below two modes at stage 2-3, SN L-L). The in-world alarm mark is TRUTH, untagged, and can never be added, suppressed or faked by a lie (R14; SN L-A): it is the one surface where the fantasy promises "if this shows, believe it". The promise is one-directional: its presence is the ship speaking and outranks the needle; its absence proves nothing. It appears only where the alarm-eligible subject itself is (IW-19), so believing it still costs the walk to get there. Honest tremor and the reduced-motion stress notch appear only on an honest reading (R9, R19), so "shake = real" is a rule the game never breaks. Under reduced motion the lie stays distinguishable: never-rest and the continuous digit tick remain, glide scaling is the Filter's (PF-39), settle becomes a step, tremor becomes a held notch that is never shown on a lying reading.
105	
106	**What must never happen (named as rule violations).** An honest gauge that glides; a lying gauge that settles or trembles; a card that disagrees with its gauge in either direction; a lie that ends with a snap or a cue (the end is never announced, SN-16); any surface that lets a player read their sanity off an instrument (a gauge that always lies near a stage threshold, a colour correlated with stage; PF-38).
107	
108	### Tone and language
109	
110	Quiet, mechanical, intimate. Instruments are the calmest thing on screen until they are not: the honest instrument is reassurance with weight (settle, rest), the lying one is an itch (it never rests). Dread lives in the gap between the two, never in UI energy (ART 7.3 rejected "juicy UI"). The register used in this GDD and in player-facing keys: *reading, needle, zone, glass, bezel, housing, face, sight-glass, meniscus, digit, settle, tremor, glide, tick, hold stale, rest, witness, second instrument, second opinion, falsify, check, chest lamp, beam, Chemlight glowstick, fixture, lantern pool.* Not used outside a REJECT or guard-rail line: status, health, condition, indicator, meter, bar (except "linear bar" quoted from ART 3.4), animate, tween, bounce, real/fake, true/false icon, "detected", "spotted", "hallucination" in player-facing text, "hand lamp", and the words OK, FAILED, DEGRADED, WORN, LOW, CRITICAL on any card or gauge. The card label is a stencilled ship label — the reading's name on its fitting, caps, Hull Grey on Ground — closer to a part number painted on a pipe than a tooltip; exact strings are the narrative-director's and the localisation lead's, and every string is a `tr()` StringName key (IA-39).

147	- Players describe a glide in their own words as "wandering", "drifting" or "won't settle" and a tremor as "shaking" (the motion grammar is legible without colour).

No cooldown is proposed (it would be an unexplained rule).
150	- *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Beat C attribution.** After a lethal remote-lie death, at least 4 of 6 testers (a D95 default) attribute it to ignoring the leak (the gauge's wander, fringe or tick) or the witness (the hiss, the draught), and at most 1 of 6 call it unfair. Coding rule: the tester's first unprompted explanation is coded as LEAK/WITNESS (own fault), GAUGE-ONLY (the lie alone, no leak or witness named) or OTHER; the protocol is a post-death one-question prompt, "what happened?", asked before any hint. A failure of this criterion is a Sanity/witness-clarity signal, not a reason to remove the lethal lie.
