152	## Detailed Design
153	
154	### Core Rules
155	
156	*Conventions.* Rules are named `IW-n` (In-World); each states a **Rule** (what the player sees and the contract with neighbours), a **Why** and **Edge notes**. Formulas are `D.n` (Formulas section: D.1 needle angle, D.2 zone intervals, D.3 honest numeral, D.4 settle, D.5 tremor, D.6 card layout, D.7 legibility table, D.8 instrument budget, D.9 gleam edge, D.10 reduced-motion substitutes, D.11 linear instruments, D.12 `lsb` visibility lint). Conflicts are `K-n` (K-1..K-14 from the brief, K-15 and K-16 raised by the ux-designer, K-17 and K-18 raised in this stage); open questions `OQ-IW-n`. "(advisor ruling Rn)", "(checkpoint ruling Cn)" and "(Xn)" are provenance labels from the authoring run: the `rulings.md` they cite is not on disk and **no rulings digest exists in this document**; the rule each label governs is stated in the clause or rule that cites it, and a label is never the only statement of a rule *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (the earlier claim that a digest at the end of Open Questions restates every ruling was false and is withdrawn); "(orchestrator ruling: ...)" marks a place where two specialists disagreed and this GDD picked one. Values that are this GDD's own and not yet registered are `[PLACEHOLDER]`; values quoted from a neighbour carry their owner and are never changed here. Implementation choices are tagged "-> ADR candidate" and kept out of the rules. **Chest-lamp sweep:** the beam origin is the per-facing chest point (PC); the lamp is hands-free; thrown Chemlight glowsticks (`#86B896`) light a gauge exactly as the beam does; no "hand lamp" wording appears anywhere in this document.
157	
158	**Rule index.** Group A, what this system is: IW-1 ownership, IW-2 presentation-only, IW-3 lit-only readability, IW-4 housing pip, IW-5 reading source. Group B, the instrument family: IW-6 taxonomy, IW-7 dial template, IW-8 data and calibration record, IW-9 quantity set, IW-10 the needle element. Group C, honest motion: IW-11 continuous change and settle, IW-12 tremor, IW-13 motion-mode dispatch, IW-14 readouts, IW-15 zone bands. Group D, lying surfaces and state frames: IW-16 the gleam, IW-17 Module-Body Presenter, IW-18 WORN, IW-19 alarm mark, IW-20 sight-glass and linear instruments. Group E, the inspect view: IW-21 targeting, IW-22 card content, IW-23 placement, IW-24 lifecycle, IW-25 input and falsification, IW-26 parity. Group F, boundaries: IW-27 reduced motion, IW-28 never-do list, IW-29 manifest floors, IW-30 DEAD binding, IW-31 placement record, IW-32 sound, IW-33 pause and restore, IW-34 fallbacks, IW-35 flagged not edited, IW-36 legibility contract, IW-37 strings, IW-38 diagnostics.
159	
160	#### Group A. What this system is
161	
162	**IW-1. Ownership: module-body reading surfaces.**
163	*Rule.* In-World Instruments owns (a) every gauge, dial, level sight-glass and state glyph produced by the ship or a derelict, drawn as lit sprites on layer 0; (b) the inspect card on layer 2, the same instrument at HUD size; (c) the **Module-Body Presenter**: the selection among a module sheet's *honest* state frames and the drawing of the state glyph (IW-17). It owns no module art (Item DB `sprite_family` names the sheet and state tokens), no placement (Layout and Derelict Authoring), no behaviour of the module, and no decision about whether, when, for whom or by how much anything lies (Filter and Sanity). It never calls `true_value`. Every reading produced by the ship or a derelict is this GDD's; Suit & Equipment and HUD & Suit Layer own only suit-produced and hand-tool readings (advisor ruling R7, R24).
164	*Why.* IDX:39 and ART 7.0 ("the ship is an instrument": who produced the number decides where it is drawn). No sibling claims the presenter (DA:1340, FT:232, IA:920, PF:1461). DA:1571's row assigning "gauges and instruments reading authored systems" to "the suit and HUD" is a stale assignment, refreshed by its owner (K-4).
165	*Edge notes.* The index has no row naming the module presenter (K-11): flagged to the producer, not edited here (IW-35).
166	
167	**IW-2. Presentation-only, zero registrations.**
168	*Rule.* Instruments are `PRESENTATION` subscribers (KRN:106-110; PIPE PR-8). They read `SIM` and `PERCEPTION_OUT` views and write only CanvasItem, Material, Light2D, particle and audio-request state; never a block, a command, a hook or a mutator. A notification is a dirty mark; reading and drawing happen in the render callback; placement is integer base px; nothing here can cause a tick. The card is **not** an `INPUT_SURFACE`: it issues no commands. The Controller's Adapter (an `INPUT_SURFACE`) owns the `inspect_card` context and publishes a presentation-local signal `{context, inspect_ref}` (registry: `inspect_card_context_signal`) that Instruments subscribe to (IW-25). Instruments register no block, hook, mutator, dirty key or persisted field (advisor ruling R22; K-1).
169	*Why.* PR-8 rule 1 (PIPE:188): `INPUT_SURFACE` only "if it also issues commands — the HUD's prompts do not; the chart table does" (PIPE's example only: per Chart Table CT-27, the chart table holds the `INPUT_SURFACE` class for VS-B and submits nothing at MVP). Instruments submit nothing.
170	*Edge notes.* Refresh owed by the Controller: PC-16 (PC:147: "an `INPUT_SURFACE` of In-World Instruments"), PC:77's purpose column ("Interaction's inspect verb", contradicting IA-38), PC:210 row 10 (K-1, K-12).
171	
172	**IW-3. Lit-only readability: "What You Light, You Can Read".**
173	*Rule.* A world gauge is readable exactly as far as the world lighting makes its pixels visible: Instruments do **not** gate the drawing of a world gauge on `lit(ref)`; the lit renderer and the HullSurface material make an unlit face dark. Two things are gated on the Emitter State bit `lit(ref)` (hysteresis `LIT_ON_PM` 150 / `LIT_OFF_PM` 120, no dwell; owner technical-artist; EM-22): the **inspect prompt** (Interaction's, IW-21) and the **inspect card** (IW-24). No instrument is an emitter and no gauge is a lantern. Mechanical gauges need no power to be read at MVP, so a dead loop's gauge shows its reading as soon as light reaches it. Thrown Chemlight glowsticks and fixtures light a gauge as the beam does.
174	*Why.* P3: reading spends light. Gating the card by the sim bit and the face by the renderer keeps one source of light truth each (ART 7.0 "unreadable until lit"; LO:436; EM:864).
175	*Edge notes.* Between `LIT_OFF_PM` and `LIT_ON_PM` the face may be dimly visible while the card is refused: intended (precision costs more light than a glance). Gauge motion is updated whether or not the face is lit (cheap, and a face entering the beam shows its current needle on its first lit frame); the gleam is "lit with its host" and needs no lit query (PF-16). The face is never shown or hidden by `lit(ref)` in code, so the 150/120 hysteresis cannot make a face flash at a pool edge (HR-13); only the prompt and the card are lit-gated, and the card needs a fresh press to reopen. Whether a gauge needs power at a later tier is OQ-IW-11.
176	
177	**IW-4. Self-emission is a non-readable housing pip, and the pip is corruptible.**
178	*Rule.* "A running loop's gauge is faintly lit by its own emission" (ART 7.0) is realised as a small loop-hue **housing pip** (size `[PLACEHOLDER]`, 4x2 art px proposed by the art-director, 2x2 by the ux-designer; OQ-IW-12) on the emissive layer (mask bit 2, casts no light, exposes nothing; LO-14, LO:225). It exists only while the bound subject's `served_pm` > 0, lets the player *find* a running gauge in the dark, and does **not** make the face readable and does **not** make `lit(ref)` true. It is drawn through the `HOUSING_GLOW(ref)` ref, so it is stage-2 corruptible: finding a gauge by its pip is not proof its loop runs. Its emission is capped at or below fixture glow and well below the beam (`PIP_EMIT_MAX`, set by the Lighting spike, ART 8.12); the hull/integrity loop has no pip (it has no running medium) (advisor ruling R21; K-6).
179	*Why.* Keeps `lit(ref)`, the card, Sanity's lit-entry and P3 consistent without adding emitters or an Emitter State change (LO-14's channel rule: "a lamp housing's own emissive sprite ... read the Filter channel and may lie").
180	*Edge notes.* The pip carries **presence or absence only** ("something here is running"); loop identity is the housing's fitting silhouette (IW-7), so the hue-removed test is met by silhouette and by the pip's on/off state. The fixture lamp's brightness from `served_pm` is consequence channel and is never confused with the pip, which casts no pool.
181	
182	**IW-5. Reading source: one pull per instrument per frame; never cache; never read truth.**
183	*Rule.* In the render callback each on-screen instrument in a loaded section obtains its displayed value with exactly one `perceived(ref, viewer)` call (PF-7), `viewer` being the local seat's `PlayerId`; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* one **`InstrumentPresenter` per instrument** is the sole caller of `perceived()` for its ref and the sole owner of the settle, tremor, dwell and notch scalars, and the wall node and the card are views of the frame index and digits it publishes once per frame (the Filter's `(ref, viewer, frame)` memo is the backstop; ADR candidate, X-6). An instrument never stores a `Perceived` record across frames, never addresses the Filter by `peer_id` (PF-10), and never calls `true_value`, `summary()` (a ship-status read), `power_use()` (Attention's stimulus) or `can_join()`. It may read `read_view` only for **non-value** inputs: the tremor predicate (IW-12), module frame selection and WORN (IW-17, IW-18), the alarm predicate (IW-19), and binding validity (IW-30). Those reads are refreshed once per Graph step (`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6), not per frame, and never feed a displayed value. The needle target is `displayed_pm`. An instrument that is off-screen or in an unloaded section pulls nothing; on its first pull after being culled it **snaps** to `displayed_pm` with no settle and no interpolation from stale history (history older than one Graph step is meaningless, and a settle on re-entry would be a motion with no world cause, P1) (advisor ruling R18).
184	*Why.* PF-8: the record never contains the truth while a lie is active; caching would let a stale record outlive a lie's end. R18 and PF-3: only the Filter wraps a true value.
185	*Edge notes.* Presentation-local scalars (the settle triple, `prev_honest_pm` and the rest, window and reversal-dwell scalars of IW-11, tremor onset and decay timestamps, the numeral throttle timestamp) are derived drawing state, not cached `Perceived` records: each is a pure function of values the player was already shown, none is read by another system, all are discarded on restore, cull and camera cut. **CONFLICT K-17 (new): LSG:998 and LS-20 (LSG:201) (locked) say "gauges read `read_view` at render rate for smooth needles" (LS-20: "Instruments and Audio poll `read_view` at render rate for smooth needles")**, which contradicts R18/PF-3 (a gauge never reads a value from `read_view`). This GDD follows R18 and PF-3: value reads go only through `perceived`; the "smooth needles" of LSG:998 and LS-20 is delivered by IW-11's interpolation, not by a value read. The Graph's own sentences are routed to its owner as a refresh. Related: the honest path carries no previous value, which IW-11 answers with the local scalar `prev_honest_pm` (K-17, checkpoint ruling C14).

205	**IW-7. Dial template family: two authored sizes, one arc.**
206	*Rule.* All dials use `arc_deg` 240 (open sector at the bottom; the arc runs -120 to +120 degrees clockwise from 12 o'clock). Two authored sizes (registry: `dial_size_class`): **DIAL_L** `needle_len_px` 24 in a 96x48 prop cell and **DIAL_S** `needle_len_px` 18 in a 48x48 cell. Both are at or above `NEEDLE_LEN_MIN_PX` 16 (owner: this GDD; value unchanged, range 14.3-32) and glide-eligible: `rate_floor` = max(0.5, 28.6 / `needle_len_px`) = 1.19 deg/s at 24 and 1.59 deg/s at 18, inside the 0.5-2.0 band (PF-13, PF-17). Loop identity is the housing's fitting silhouette (ART 3.4, 7.2 table) plus the running-only pip, never dial geometry or face hue. Geometry (art px; pivot at the arc centre; band inner radius = needle length + 1; one geometry set, fixed by checkpoint ruling C5; the pixel mock S-A1 confirms the DIAL_S bezel only):
207	
208	| Size | Needle | Band inner r | Band thickness | Outer r | Arc width (2 x outer r) | Arc height (1.5 x outer r) | Housing (DIAL_L bezel 2 px, DIAL_S bezel 1 px, each side) | Cell | Cell margin |

210	| DIAL_L | 24 | 25 | 3 | 28 | 56 | 42 | 60 x 46 | 96x48 | 36 px horizontal, 2 px vertical |
211	| DIAL_S | 18 | 19 | 3 | 22 | 44 | 33 | 46 x 35 (bezel 1 px each side) | 48x48 | 1 px each side horizontally, 13 px vertically in total |

213	*Arithmetic.* A 240-degree arc centred on 12 o'clock reaches its full width at the 3 and 9 o'clock points (|x| = r) and its lowest point at the end stops (y = r cos 120 = -0.5 r), so height = r (above the pivot) + 0.5 r (below) = 1.5 r. Needle stroke is 2 art px (HR-12: a stroke is at least 2 screen px at every `k`). The outer radius is the band's inner radius plus its thickness: DIAL_L 25 + 3 = 28 (arc 2 x 28 = 56 wide, 1.5 x 28 = 42 high, housing 56 + 4 = 60 by 42 + 4 = 46 with a 2 px bezel), DIAL_S 19 + 3 = 22 (arc 2 x 22 = 44 wide, 1.5 x 22 = 33 high, housing 44 + 2 = 46 by 33 + 2 = 35 with a 1 px bezel). The DIAL_S band is **3 rows** because IW-15 needs three patterns (solid, hatched, notched) that can be told apart; a 2-row band could not carry them. In the 48x48 cell the DIAL_S housing leaves 48 - 46 = 2 px horizontally (1 px each side) and 48 - 35 = 13 px vertically in total; DIAL_L leaves 96 - 60 = 36 px horizontally and 48 - 46 = 2 px vertically. The 1-px DIAL_S bezel is a minimum-feature exception routed to the art-director under BR-9 (ART 5.6); S-A1 confirms the bezel only, the radii are fixed. **Helmet-scale test (ART:714; the crewmate helmet is a 16 px circle; a round feature must be < 5.3 or > 32 art px):** sweep diameter 2L = 48 (DIAL_L) and 36 (DIAL_S), outer arc diameter 56 (DIAL_L) and **44** (DIAL_S, > 32), hub 4 (< 5.3): all pass. A dial at exactly `NEEDLE_LEN_MIN_PX` 16 has a 32 px sweep, on the boundary, so 16 is the Filter's eligibility floor and **not an authored size** (advisor ruling R25). The dial is never a closed circle; the 3.1 silhouette test is run on both housings (AC-IW-9). **Mounting (orchestrator ruling: art-director's terminal-fitting rule adopted over the ux-designer's housing-over-fitting-cell proposal).** Neither dial fits inside the pipe band (rows 29-58 of the 72 px face; ART 6.3 rule 7): DIAL_L (46 high) is a cap-less wall-hung panel or machine-panel instrument and is never mounted on a pipe run; DIAL_S (35 high) attaches at a pipe's **terminal fitting** (pipes never dead-end without one, ART 6.3 rule 1), centred on the band's mid-row (43.5, spanning about rows 26-61), so "pipe -> gauge" reads as a sentence; the exception to ART 6.3 rule 7 ("except an instrument seated on a terminal fitting") is a bible refresh owed by the art-director (BR-2). A MACHINE_PANEL dial of either size sits inside the module's 96x96 node. Wall gauges take the host face's sort origin (PIPE:129, :137). (advisor ruling R6, R25; K-7)
214	*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Lower-sector arithmetic (the fitting plate).** The open sector below the pivot is bounded by the rays 60 degrees either side of straight down, so at depth `y` below the pivot its half-width is `y x tan 60` = 1.732 `y`; its floor is the arc's lowest points, at `y` = 0.5 x outer r (14 on DIAL_L, 11 on DIAL_S), and the housing's outer bottom edge is that plus the bezel (16 and 12). A plate of half-width `w` needs its top row at `y` >= `w` / 1.732. DIAL_L: the 16-px plate (`w` 8) starts at row 5 (4.62 rounded up), and the earlier 12-px height would end at row 17, 2.62 px past the arc floor and 1 px past the outer edge; the plate is therefore **16x11**, seated on the bottom bezel and ending exactly on the outer edge at row 16. DIAL_S: the 12-px plate (`w` 6) starts at row 4 (3.46 rounded up) and the 8-px height ends at row 12, exactly the outer edge (1-px bezel), so **12x8 stands**, also seated on the bezel. Both plates overlay the bottom bezel and overflow nothing; S-A1 confirms the silhouettes at 16x11 and 12x8. The LINEAR bead is **6 wide x 2 tall** (the width of the 6-px tube); the earlier "2x6" read as 2 wide x 6 tall, which fits neither the tube nor the 4-px caps. With a 54-px interior and `travel_px` 50 the bead spans rows 0-1 at empty and 50-51 at full, clear of both caps. Plate and bead extents are in the S-A1 scope.

216	*Why.* Concept: solo-developer art load; PF-45: one calibration per kind.
217	*Edge notes.* Fallback if the silhouette test reads "gauge on a console" as the crewmate-reserved composition (ART 6.6 rule 2): a squarer, octagonal-chamfered arc authored once for both sizes (R-A2). If the terminal-fitting mount is rejected: dials only on MACHINE_PANEL mounts and the wall carries sight-glasses only. DIAL_L consumes 46 of 48 rows (a 1-px margin each side): it cannot be a console-face detail inside a cap-plus-face prop; this is a placement constraint routed to Layout and Derelict Authoring (IW-31).

219	**IW-8. Instrument data and the calibration record (the answer to PF-45).**
220	*Rule.* Per instrument surface, a record in `assets/data/instruments/`: `instrument_id`; `gauge_kind` (DIAL | LINEAR | READOUT | GLYPH | FRAME); `size_class`; `quantity` (IW-9); `arc_deg` (DIAL; 0 for LINEAR); `needle_len_px` (DIAL) or `travel_px` (LINEAR meniscus travel); `value_lo`, `value_hi`, `lsb`, `unit_key`, `name_key` (the card label); `zones[]` as LS-7 band **names** mapped to a pattern class (D.2; the thresholds are derived at build time and never written into this data); `lie_surface_id` per corruptible surface (`<instrument_id>.needle`, `.glyph`, `.housing_glow`, `.machine_frame`; there is no `.readout` surface and the card has no id of its own: one ref carries one lie and one `Perceived`, so the card numeral is `displayed_value` of the `.needle` ref's `Perceived`, and `motion_mode` TICK and STALE apply to that numeral, checkpoint ruling C2); and `beyond_witness`, the flag set defined below, which is **derived from placement and quantity** and must equal the authored value (lint `BEYOND_WITNESS_MISMATCH`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The binding (`node_ref` or `room_key`, `mount`, `host_face` and, since the design review, `mount_room`, `subject_room`, `host_node`) is **placement data** authored in Layout and Derelict Authoring (IW-31). A missing or malformed record yields the honest path plus `lie_unrenderable` (PF-44), a **build failure** for any kind listed in `lie_targets.json`. Assets owed exactly as PF V.11: `mach_gauge_<loop>_alb.png` plus `_msk.png` with slices `glass`, `needle_edge`, `needle`; a `ui_` sheet with a `glass` slice for digit cells and card glass; `mach_<name>_<state>_alb.png`; `mach_lamp_<name>_lit` / `_unlit`; both honest state frames of every pair on **one sheet page** (advisor ruling R11; PF-45). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, answers Perception Filter PF-9 join)* **Join to Sanity's `subject_ref` `{stable_id, surface}` (SN-23).** `stable_id` is the module's stable id and equals the IW-8 `instrument_id` (lint: one-to-one). The surface enum maps to the facets above: 1 NEEDLE maps to `.needle`; 2 READOUT maps to the `.needle` facet of an instrument whose `gauge_kind` is READOUT (a digit-only instrument has no needle sprite, but its single lie facet is that ref, whose `displayed_value` is the numeral); 3 GLYPH to `.glyph`; 4 GLOW_SPRITE to `.housing_glow`; 5 MACHINE_SPRITE to `.machine_frame`. The ref's `quantity`, `node_ref` or `room_key` come from this record, never from the `subject_ref`. The record supplies both an OK and an alarm interval (PF-45) so the Filter can derive the GLIDE dial side. Lint `LIE_SURFACE_ENUM_MISMATCH`: a surface whose facet is absent from the record is a build failure.
221	*Definitions: mount, subject and `beyond_witness`.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier text declared `beyond_witness` in {REMOTE, MAGNITUDE, TREND} without defining any value, and the manifest tagged instruments REMOTE that hang in the room they read.)* Placement splits the two places an instrument has. `mount_room` is the compartment in which the housing physically hangs; `subject_room` is the compartment holding what the reading is about (for a compartment ref the named `cid`; for a node ref the compartment that holds the node, found through `nodes_in(cid)`; for a POWER `loop_component` ref the compartment of its anchor node). `host_node` is the node whose own panel or prop carries the housing (none for a WALL_FACE mount) and `subject_node` is the bound node (none for a compartment ref). `hops(a, b)` is the shortest path over `neighbors(cid)` (LS-19) and `hops(a, a)` = 0. `beyond_witness` is a **set of flags computed by a lint from placement and quantity; nobody judges it, and the authored field must equal the computed set**:
222	
223	| Flag | Predicate (testable) | Reading for the player | Manifest example |
224	|---|---|---|---|
225	| REMOTE | `hops(mount_room, subject_room)` >= 1. A REMOTE instrument is lie-eligible only if also `hops` <= `WITNESS_HOPS_MAX` 2: SN L-W measures the witness from the lying surface's compartment (the mount) to the fault's compartment (the subject), so the same pair of rooms decides it | The dial is about a room the player is not standing in, and its witness (frost, hiss, draught) is not at hand. It is the only flag that can produce Beat C, because L-G forbids a FALSE_OK only on the quantity of the compartment the seat stands in | `inst_a_machine_T` (1 hop) |
226	| MAGNITUDE | `hops` = 0 and the quantity's LS-22 witness is band-stepped (O2: the THIN and HYPOXIC body cues; pressure: draught present or strong; coolant and fuel: the drip and the puddle), so the dial adds where the value sits inside a band. A quantity whose LS-22 witness is continuous (`T`: frost reach; `load`: lamp brightness and hum pitch) is never MAGNITUDE | The witness says that something is wrong; the dial says how much | `inst_airlock_P` |
227	| TREND | the quantity is `T` or `stock`: inertial quantities that move over minutes, whose witness shows a state and not a direction or a rate (frost does not say that the room is warming) | The dial shows which way the value is going | `inst_cryo_bay_T` |

Flags combine (`inst_a_machine_T` is REMOTE and TREND).

232	*Why.* The Filter "cannot invent geometry" (PF-45 rationale); gameplay values are data-driven (coding standards); one calibration per kind.
233	*Edge notes.* No violet or flesh is ever baked in a `ui_` or `_alb` sheet (reserved-hue scan, ART:1207); the gleam is produced at runtime (IW-16). The face art with its zone arcs is generated at build time from this data and the LS-7 band names -> ADR candidate (build tool). A record whose `arc_deg` is not 240 or whose `needle_len_px` is below `NEEDLE_LEN_MIN_PX` fails a build lint (one dial family; glide eligibility). The zone-band lint, the `lsb` visibility lint and the quantity-collision lint (IW-9) are specified in D.2, D.12 and AC-IW-12, AC-IW-23. All records are lint-checked against `lie_targets.json` coverage (AC-SN-45): every module kind needs at least one tagged corruptible surface.

235	**IW-9. The quantity set and ref addressing.**
236	*Rule.* The closed MVP quantity set (registry: `instrument_quantity`); each row names the Graph source, unit, span, `lsb` and band family. Bands are LS-7 and LSG D.9, consumed by name and never redefined; spans are this GDD's gauge spans `[PLACEHOLDER]` pending the Graph's LS-26 nominals:
237	
238	| `quantity` | Graph source (`read_view`) | Unit shown | `value_lo` .. `value_hi` | `lsb` | Zone family | Kind |
239	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
240	| `p_o2` | `compartment(cid).p_o2` | kPa (value / 10), one decimal | 0 .. 300 dkPa | 1 dkPa | LS-7 `p_o2` bands | DIAL |
241	| `P` | `compartment(cid).P` | kPa, whole | 0 .. 1100 dkPa | 10 dkPa | LS-7 `P` bands | DIAL |
242	| `T` | `compartment(cid).T` | whole degrees C (mC / 1000) | -60000 .. 90000 mC | 1000 mC | LS-7 `T` bands (7 bands) | DIAL_L only |
243	| `stock` | `node(id).stock_pm` (the Graph's `⌊1000 × stock / capacity⌋`, capacity = the def's `cap_ml`, `BATT_CELL` or the O2_TANK template maximum; `true_value` kind `stock_pm`, LS-19 additions) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | percent | 0 .. 1000 permille | 10 permille | none (an empty-end tick only) | LINEAR (tank, reservoir) or DIAL_S (battery) |
244	| `load` | the Graph's `load_pm` `true_value` kind for a POWER `loop_component` (**requested**, specified below; this is not LSG `rho`, which is per edge and built from served-power sums) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | percent of supply | 0 .. 1250 permille | 10 permille | high edge at 1000 pm is this GDD's calibration (the brownout, D.6 `sat` < 1000), not an LS-7 band | DIAL |
245	| `strain` (held out of the MVP manifest, provisional) | `node(id).hp` inverted | an engineering-unit key, never a percent | 0 .. 10000 bp | 250 bp (the dirty quantum) | `HP_OK` 7000 / `HP_FAIL` 3000 edges | DIAL |

247	*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **The `load` reading is a Graph-published quantity, not an Instruments derivation.** LS-19 publishes `supply` and `demand` as `true_value` kinds and calls their ratio "Instruments' own reading", but the Filter can only wrap a `true_value` and IW-5 forbids Instruments deriving a value outside the Filter, so a derived `load` had no lie path and no dirty-key quantum. The chosen path is **(a): the Graph publishes `load_pm` as a `true_value` kind** (request OQ-IW-20; cross-GDD note to the Life-Support Graph). Specification: `load_pm` = 0 when `supply` = 0, and `min(1250, floor(1000 x demand / supply))` otherwise; the clamp to the span belongs to the publisher, so `displayed_pm` is always inside 0..1000 and `diag.instr_pm_clamped` stays a defect counter. **Three bus cases, no longer folded into one pegged reading.** *Dead* (`supply` 0, `demand` > 0): the needle rests at the low stop, there is no housing pip (the pip needs `served_pm` > 0), the lamps are dark and the hum is silent, so the player is told that nothing is carried and not that the bus is overloaded. *Idle* (`supply` > 0, `demand` 0): the same low stop with the pip lit, so dead and idle are told apart by the pip and the lamps and not by the needle. *Loaded or overloaded* (`supply` > 0): 1..1250, with the NOTCHED stop from 1000. **Dirty cadence:** `load_pm` rides the loop key `L/<loop>/<anchor>` with a quantum of `LOAD_QUANTUM_PERMILLE` 20 (proposed; Graph-owned like the other LS-20 quanta; 16 pm of the 0..1250 span, 1.6 px on DIAL_L). The Filter wraps `load_pm` like any other kind: a lie moves the needle on the Filter's glide band and carries the full tri-modal leak. Until the Graph grants `load_pm`, `inst_engine_bus_load` is not buildable as a lie target (it is TRUTH-default by floor (i) in any case, so no manifest count moves). **Interim path (b), if the Graph declines:** the Filter's wrap derives the identical expression from `true_value(supply)` and `true_value(demand)` of the same component inside its one wrap point and states how lie and leak apply to the derived value; Instruments never derive.

249	`strain` is held out because a hull-condition dial risks becoming a condition bar in disguise (BS-6, FT-4, IDB): it ships only if the Graph confirms a physical stress quantity that is not `hp` (OQ-IW-5). Coolant **temperature** is not a quantity: no `read_view` field carries it (`T` is a compartment atmosphere value), so coolant instruments are level (`stock`) readings only until the Graph publishes one. **Ref addressing.** A node-bound instrument uses `GRAPH_NODE(kind, id)`; a room instrument uses `GRAPH_COMPARTMENT(cid, quantity)` (registry `perceived_query` `ref_union`; the Filter adopted the `quantity` term at the 2026-10-27 consistency pass, PF-9), so two lie-eligible compartment instruments in one room are distinct in PF-7's `(ref, viewer, frame)` memo. **Adopted by the Filter (PF-9, OQ-PF-29):** the `quantity` term and the LINEAR branch. **Confirmed by the Graph (LS-19 additions, 2026-10-27):** the `true_value(kind, id)` kinds are `p_o2`, `P`, `T` (compartment), `stock_pm` (node), `supply` and `demand` (POWER component), plus `hp` for diagnostics, and the former fallback of one lie-eligible compartment instrument per room is retired. Two instruments with the same `(subject, quantity)` still share one ref and so one lie, which would not be a second opinion; the lint `INSTR_QUANTITY_COLLISION` therefore fails the build for a duplicated `(subject_room or subject_node, quantity)` pair. `load_pm` is requested (above). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (advisor ruling R12; K-5, resolved)
250	*Why.* The registry formula `atmosphere_derive` lists this GDD in its `referenced_by`; the Graph does not enumerate `true_value` kinds anywhere (grep of LSG and PF found none).
251	*Edge notes.* The `T` gauge in `cryo_bay` is lie-eligible beside the `p_o2` dial now that the fallback is retired (IW-29) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The ui-programmer's alternative ids (`p_total`, `temp`, `bus_load`, `store_level`) are not used; the ids mirror the Graph's field names (orchestrator ruling).

253	**IW-10. The needle element.**
254	*Rule.* A needle is a **separate pivoted element** (never part of the face art) whose tip is placed on whole art pixels at integer base-px positions with nearest-neighbour sampling, 2 art px thick; the tip moves in whole art pixels: one pixel step corresponds to 9.95 pm on DIAL_L and 13.3 pm on DIAL_S (D.1). No instrument draws any element with a drawn line or an anti-aliased edge: the pinned engine's `CanvasItem` line drawing carries no antialiasing feather in 4.7 (`[REF]` breaking-changes.md), so a drawn needle would be thinner than authored and PF-45's separate-needle requirement unmet. Zone bands, ticks and bezel arcs are authored sprites baked into the face at build time, never drawn at runtime. The needle's wander (Filter-supplied) and tremor (IW-12) are real whole-pixel tip flips, not shimmer.
255	*Why.* 4.7 engine fact; PF-45; ART 7.3.
256	*Edge notes.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Decision (baseline): pre-rendered needle frames indexed by the rounded tip pixel, drawn with NEAREST filtering and no runtime rotation.** The build tool enumerates the distinct rounded tip positions along the arc (about 100 on DIAL_L and 76 on DIAL_S: the arc length `needle_len_px` x 4.19) and bakes one 2-px needle frame per tip pixel; a frame index is the only thing the presenter changes. The wall needle and the card needle read the **same frame index, computed once per frame by the instrument's presenter**, in a fixed order (read `perceived()`, advance the scalars, compute the tip pixel, publish one index), so wall and card parity holds by construction. A runtime-rotated `Sprite2D` stays the fallback only if spike S-A3 (OQ-IW-7, `[UNV]`: no engine-reference file covers rotation under NEAREST at `k` 1..8) shows the frame strip over budget. The Filter-facing contract is identical either way (pivot at the dial centre, `needle_len_px` the authored tip radius). A card needle is the same angle set as the wall needle, not a finer rotation (IW-26). The ADR is X-6 item 7.

260	**IW-11. Continuous change and the honest settle (closed form).**
261	*Rule.* Everything in this rule applies **only when `motion_mode` is HONEST**. (a) **Continuous change.** Honest samples of `displayed_pm` arrive when the Filter's honest memo is invalidated (an LS-20 quantum crossing, at most once per Graph step, `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6); while the Graph value sits inside one quantum there is no sample. **For MVP the honest needle's resolution is the LS-20 quantum** (checkpoint ruling C14): each instrument keeps one presentation-local scalar `prev_honest_pm` (the scalar that extends the triple of (c), beside the native-unit `prev_honest_native` that D.3 formats the card numeral from *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*); a new honest sample is drawn as a ramp from `prev_honest_pm` to the new accepted `target_pm` (the sample after the reversal dwell of (b); equal to `displayed_pm` unless a one-quantum reversal is still held) over one Graph step (100 ms) through the single PR-8 rule-5 interpolator (`tick_alpha`), with no overshoot and no extrapolation, and the needle then rests. The drawn value therefore lags the true value by at most one Graph step plus the quantum, except for a genuine one-quantum reversal, which the reversal dwell of (b) holds for `INSTR_REVERSAL_DWELL_STEPS` more steps (at most 500 ms in all) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the consequence channel tolerates both (AAV-17 requires direction agreement, not phase). A slow honest ramp reads as a mechanical detent (step, then rest), which strengthens "honest rests, the lie never rests"; a fast ramp (a decompression) crosses a quantum every step and reads as continuous. The quanta in needle terms (D.1, D.4): `p_o2` 5 dkPa over a 300 dkPa span is 16.7 pm, 1.7 px on DIAL_L and 1.25 px on DIAL_S; `P` 10 dkPa over 1100 is 9.1 pm; `T` 1000 mC over 150000 is 6.7 pm; `stock` 20 pm is 1 px at `travel_px` 50. `INSTR_SETTLE_JUMP_PM` 40 exceeds every single-quantum step (the largest is `p_o2`, 16.7 pm), so one quantum crossing never fires a settle on any quantity; on the one `settle_eligible` quantity, `load` (quantum `LOAD_QUANTUM_PERMILLE` 20 permille = 16.0 pm, D.1), three quanta accumulated inside the jump window (3 x 16 = 48 pm, over the 40 pm threshold; two = 32 pm, under it) do, see (b); the same three `p_o2` quanta (17 + 17 + 16 = 50 pm) are drawn by the D.1 ramp, because `settle_eligible` is false for `p_o2` (D.4). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G4: conforms to the per-quantity `settle_eligible` gate of D.4)* (b) **Rest, jump and settle: rest is defined in time.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier text defined rest per Graph step here and per sample in D.4 and AC-IW-17, a definition under which the settle could never fire on `p_o2` or `stock`.)* An instrument is **at rest** iff no honest sample has arrived for `INSTR_REST_STEPS` consecutive Graph steps (3 steps = 300 ms) and no settle is active; IW-11, D.4, E-IW-8, AC-IW-17 and the REST state of S2 all use this one definition. The first honest sample after rest opens a **jump window** of `INSTR_SETTLE_WINDOW_STEPS` Graph steps (4 steps = 400 ms) and records `rest_pm`, the value the needle held at rest. A *jump*, on a `settle_eligible` quantity only (D.4; `load` at MVP) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, is any sample inside that window with |`target_pm` - `rest_pm`| >= `INSTR_SETTLE_JUMP_PM` (the honest change accumulated since leaving rest, not the change of one step): a valve flick, a repair, an `apply_damage`, a breaker closing. The jump converts the in-flight ramp into a settle: the drawn value is the closed-form underdamped step response of D.4 as a pure function of `(from_pm, to_pm, t_jump)` and `present_time`, overshoot at most 5 % of the jump, settling to rest within 250-400 ms, then exactly still. A run that does not reach the threshold inside its window is a **sweep** (a continuing decompression crossing a quantum every step): it never settles until rest is re-entered, so a sustained ramp does not stutter. **The honest signature is therefore "step, then rest"**: every honest change is a detent-like step that ends at rest, and a real jump of at least 40 pm is a heavier damped ease; the overshoot shows as a 1-px tip flip only for jumps of 216 pm (DIAL_L) or 288 pm (DIAL_S) or more (D.4), and on the verified manifest actions only the `load` dial settles (D.4 reachability table). **Reversal dwell.** The LS-20 buckets have no hysteresis, so an honest value hovering on a quantum edge would flip the needle 1-2 px at up to 10 Hz with no stress descriptor, which reads as a tremor on a calm reading and teaches the lesson backwards. A sample that reverses the direction of the last accepted change by no more than one quantum is held as a candidate and accepted only after it has been the current sample for `INSTR_REVERSAL_DWELL_STEPS` Graph steps (4 = 400 ms); a candidate that equals the held value, or is superseded, is dropped. The needle, the card and the card numeral all use the accepted `target_pm`, so a 10 Hz dither across a quantum edge produces at most one move (AC-IW-110). (c) **State.** Exactly one `(from_pm, to_pm, t_jump)` triple per instrument plus the presentation-local scalars `prev_honest_pm` of (a) and `rest_pm`, the window start step and the dwell candidate (`target_pm`, `candidate_pm`, `t_candidate`) of (b), the triple discarded after `INSTR_SETTLE_MS`, neither ever persisted, never replicated, never read by any other *system*; the instrument's wall node and its card are two views of one instrument object and both draw from its single drawn value, which is what makes card parity (IW-26) hold. The triple, `prev_honest_pm` and the scalars of (b) are cleared by any non-HONEST frame and snapped by `hard_start` (the Filter's term, PF-33, raised by a kernel restore or `force_stage`), restore, camera cut and cull (IW-5, IW-33). The HUD's suit-arc settle (HS-14, `HUD_SETTLE_MS` 300 `[PH]`, HUD-owned; renamed there from `SETTLE_MS` after the collision, CF-HS-20) is a peer: it may cite `settle_response` (D.4) instead of restating a second curve, and this GDD's constants carry the `INSTR_` prefix so the two names never collide. (d) **Re-basing (orchestrator ruling: the ui-programmer's re-base adopted over the ux-designer's per-frame retarget, which would make the drawn value jump).** While a settle is active, any further change of the honest displayed value re-bases the triple: `from_pm` := the value currently drawn, `to_pm` := the new displayed value, `t_jump` := now; velocity is discarded (a small kink, accepted). A direction held through the pause neither re-opens the card nor is consumed by it (the card is already closed at the pause; held-input handling after a resume is the Controller's, OQ-IW-44). The IA-6 exemption "the inspect card of an already-lit instrument" means only that opening is not re-validated by `act_gate` as a command; it never permits a card on an unlit instrument (advisor ruling R4; EM-22). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*
380	*Why.* EM-22: keeping `lit` true after the light went "would be a window where the sim says lit and the world is dark, a P1 lie"; P3: precision costs staying lit.
381	*Edge notes.* `lit(ref)` is read each render frame, so a card closes at most one tick after the light goes. At a pool edge the card closes once on the first false and stays closed: no strobe (HR-13). If the focus moves to another instrument while the card is open, the card stays on its latched ref; there is no navigation between instruments at MVP. A card opens only from the `gameplay` context on a press, never because `lit` turned on while the player was in `chart_table` or `chat`. A press whose ref has no instrument record is consumed silently with a diagnostic (no error text, no sound).
382	
383	**IW-25. Card input, co-op and falsification.**
384	*Rule.* In the `inspect_card` context *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: entering the context sends `set_move_intent {NONE}` and clears the run latch but does not cancel a running channel (PC contexts note: the second-instrument check on the pipe being welded costs nothing); zoom stays reachable; `inspect`, `cancel` (X) and B close the card; the sim keeps ticking and the HUD critical strip stays live, so a breach during inspection is felt through the consequence channel. **Movement past the dead-zone closes the card and moves the avatar in the same frame; no move press is swallowed.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* Two refinements that do not reverse D94: (1) **held-at-entry latch**: a direction already held (a key or a stick octant) at the moment the context is entered is latched and is not a fresh move; it neither closes the card nor moves the avatar until it returns to neutral or changes octant, so pressing `inspect` while running does not close the card on the next frame (the latch is the Controller's, requested, OQ-IW-44); (2) **card dead-zone margin for a gamepad stick**: while the card is open the stick's effective dead-zone is `MOVE_DEADZONE + CARD_PAD_DEADZONE_MARGIN` (a tunable, default 0.10 normalised `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 0-0.25, exposed to the accessibility settings), so stick drift or a tremor in the hand does not close the card unintentionally; a stick inside the enlarged dead-zone does nothing, as inside the plain one, and a deliberate push past it closes the card and moves in the same frame. A keyboard has no margin. The earlier rule zeroed and swallowed the first move press, which with lethal friendly fire and restart from the last autosave could kill a player by eating an input, and the UI frame must never betray the player. P3's stillness cost survives because the gauge must stay in the beam: a player who steps away loses `lit` anyway. A move also interrupts a running channel as any move does (PC-7). **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): D94 ratified.** The PC context matrix is amended (`move_*` in `inspect_card`: closes the card, then live) and the Controller's GDD carries the amendment; the buffer-and-replay fallback is retired (OQ-IW-17, AC-IW-39) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. **Aim and cursor (K-14 closed 2026-10-27):** `set_aim` stays live so the chest lamp can hold the gauge lit, and the OS cursor is hidden and inert in `inspect_card` (PC-16, the PC context matrix, HS-52). The card is seat-local: never replicated, never visible to another seat, never a command; each seat's card reads `perceived(ref, its own PlayerId)`; a teammate's beam keeps `lit(ref)` true for my card (lit is world state) but my reach loss closes it. **Opening the card is not a falsification:** it is not a channel, lies identically to its gauge and so can never debunk; it calls no `record_falsification`; OQ-SN-12's INSPECT `check_kind` is reserved for any future *channelled* inspect verb (VS-A) (advisor ruling R13, R20).
385	*Why.* SN-16 / AD-C1: the card must never be a free falsifier; P4 needs a precision tool that is not a truth oracle. Answers the condition in AC-SN-111.
386	*Edge notes.* A teammate's friendly harm while the player stands still in the card context is the consequence channel's business: the player may close the card at any time at no cost, by `inspect`, `cancel` or simply by moving. Two cards cannot open per client (one seat per client).
387	
388	**IW-26. Card parity: the same instrument, not a second one.**
389	*Rule.* The card uses the **same** `PerceptionRef` as its wall gauge (there is no card ref and no card lie), reads the same `Perceived` through the same memo, shows the same drawn value (it reads the instrument's own settle triple and tremor state), the same motion mode, the same gleam parameters and the same HR-5 tri-modal tell, from stage 1. A lie that starts, ends or changes while the card is open appears on the card in the same frame as on the wall gauge, with no flash of the true value. Closing and reopening a card on an active lie shows the same `Perceived` and plays no new sound (the sound is the Filter's request on the ref, not on the card). Opening the card never replays a settle and never sweeps the needle in from zero. "Second instrument" in P4 is always a *different* gauge elsewhere, never the card. The card dial renders the same angle set as the wall needle (it must not be a more precise render of a lying value than the wall is of the same value). The card numeral is `displayed_value` of the **same** `.needle` ref's `Perceived` (checkpoint ruling C2): it is not a second lie target and carries no `lie_surface_id` of its own. In every non-HONEST mode the card needle draws `displayed_pm` verbatim (the Filter's trajectory, wander included, which never rests), while TICK (continuous tick) and STALE (held digits) govern the numeral only, so the card and the wall gauge never disagree about which motion mode is active (PF-9, PF-18, AC-PF-23; HR-14).
390	*Why.* Otherwise the card is either a free falsifier or a separate lie target.
391	*Edge notes.* The card has no module-frame surface, so if the wall shows a stage-3 `whole` frame while the module is `cracked`, the card shows only the reading and there is nothing for it to disagree with. Stress is the one honest-only difference of *form* that may arise (tremor versus the held notch under `reduced_motion`, K-18 resolved by D96); it is honest-only on both and never differs in a lie *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
392	
393	#### Group F. Boundaries, content floors and fallbacks
394	
395	**IW-27. Reduced motion and accessibility substitutes.**
396	*Rule.* With reduced motion (HR-8): honest settle becomes a **step** (drawn = `displayed_pm`); honest tremor is replaced by a **held stress notch pair** (each `max(NOTCH_PAIR_PX, ceil(NOTCH_MIN_SCREEN_PX / k))` art px, at least 4 screen px at every rung *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*), shown while the IW-12 predicate holds **and** `motion_mode` is HONEST, and never on a lying reading (it would be an oracle); the alarm mark holds solid. Glide, wander and lying-tick scaling are the Filter's (PF-39: `RM_GLIDE_SCALE` 0.6, rate floor not below 0.3 deg/s, wander never scaled, lying tick never below `LIE_TICK_MS`) and are not restated. The notch is two Void Steel nicks cut into the world bezel's top edge about 4 px either side of centre, and, on the card, two Hull Grey squares on the Ground plate above the dial *(orchestrator ruling: the art-director's placement adopted; R19 said "on the bezel", but HR-2 forbids Hull Grey on a bezel fill, so the card's notch sits on the Ground side of the dial rim)*. No setting removes a leak mode, hides the gleam or the card numeral, or adds an Attention or sanity surface. Instrument labels and the card obey the 21/15 text tier and UI scale `H`; the instrument face is a bitmap font at integer `H` only (advisor ruling R19). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **Reduce flashing defaults ON at first launch** (user ruling, D79): the card's honest numeral already rides the shared hold grid (D.3) and adds no flash surface that the default would need to suppress; under the HUD's stricter arbiter for reduce flashing (HS-47) a grid boundary may be skipped and the card shows the then-latest step at the next one, which the lag bound of `2 x HONEST_TICK_MS` already covers. Card tremor is suppressed under `reduced_motion` (IW-12, D96).
397	*Why.* HR-8: the backbone of the lie (never-rest, continuous tick) survives; tremor is the one signature that needs a static substitute.
398	*Edge notes.* Accessibility Settings (Alpha) depends on this GDD (IDX:209): its reduced-motion toggle reads the Filter's published scalars (`reduced_motion_glide_pm`, `breath_depth_pm`, `lie_tick_min_ms`) and this rule's substitute *(provisional — Accessibility Settings undesigned)*. The screen-reader text for a card (Alpha) is built from `Perceived.displayed_value` only, never `true_value`; the pinned engine's accessibility live-region maturity is `[UNV]`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Tell survival for a deaf, colour-blind player.** With the sound removed and the hue removed, a lie keeps the never-rest motion mode on the needle, the continuous tick on the card numeral and the gleam as a **luminance** fringe; the claim of at least two tells therefore holds only if the fringe `#B07BE6` keeps at least `GLEAM_LUM_CONTRAST_MIN` 3:1 (the WCAG non-text ratio, `[PLACEHOLDER]`) against the glass it rides in greyscale, measured at S-A1 and tested by AC-IW-120. **Tell-survival rule** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: for every combination of reduced motion (scale 0.6), captions on or off, greyscale or a colour-vision filter, and sound off, at least two of the three tells survive on every lying instrument: the never-resting needle (the wander is never scaled, PF-39), the luminance gleam (above `GLEAM_LUM_CONTRAST_MIN`) and the sound (not counted when sound is off or unheard). The numeral tick is a mode of the motion tell and is not counted as a separate tell. Where reduced motion lengthens a digit hold, D.12 accepts it explicitly (`T_VIS_MAX_RM_S`). Tested by AC-IW-125; the caption tier is recorded in `design/accessibility-requirements.md` once that file exists (OQ-IW-42). Captions for lie sounds (Alpha) are a gate dependency of the accessibility tier and not an Instruments feature. `design/accessibility-requirements.md` does not exist; `/ux-design accessibility` sets the tier (OQ-IW-42).

A seat that is hauling salvage then receives no lie on A at all, which is Sanity's accepted consequence of SE-11 (EC-SN-42, EC-SN-62), not a defect here; but "scan everything" must not become dominant for the seat that does carry the scanner, so the lower end is reported and the asks below make it seat-independent. **Which lies the first scanner-less seat sees.** The first lie of a world is ALARM-direction by construction (SN-16), and the alarm credits are the widest (fixed gauge, scanner, or the suit in the seat's own compartment), so the Beat B anchor (`inst_engine_room_p_o2`, fixed partner) fires for every seat; the COMFORT lies (Beat C) need a fixed partner or a usable scanner. **L-2I status of this manifest (floor (i)): satisfied by the scanner for a usable-scanner seat; satisfied without it only where a fixed partner is listed.** Fixed partners exist for the `p_o2` gauges (home: `cryo_bay` plus `engine_room`) and for the scrubber glyphs of home and B (credited by a `p_o2` gauge in another compartment); **not** for A's glyph or A's `p_o2` (the only A `p_o2` gauge is in `a_life`, the glyph's own compartment), for `T` (no second `T` gauge on any site; `suit.warmth` is an alarm-direction credit only), for `P` (no second `P` gauge; the suit credits `T` only), for `inst_engine_bus_load` (no second bus-load reading), the two coolant levels, the home fuel level or the batteries. **P0 asks to Derelict Authoring (replacing the earlier battery-partner ask, which would still leave A scanner-only):** (1) in derelict A, a second `p_o2` dial reading another compartment, for example `inst_a_spine_p_o2` mounted in and reading `a_spine`, which makes `inst_a_life_p_o2`, the new dial and `inst_scr_a_glyph` fixed-credited (A lower end 0 to 3); (2) in derelict B, a second `p_o2` dial reading another compartment, for example `inst_b_spine_p_o2` in `b_spine`, which makes the Beat C fixture `inst_b_dock_p_o2` seat-independent (B lower end 1 to 3). A `T`-loop partner for fixture A is not asked: fixture A stays scanner-dependent (OQ-IW-35). The two asked dials are owed rows and are not added to the 18 above. Counts are indicative; no pod dash (K-10). **No acceptance criterion may assert that the manifest as listed passes floor (i)** (advisor ruling R17); AC-IW-108 and AC-IW-109 run against a test-owned fixture manifest with an explicit `seat_scanner_usable` input.
429	*Why.* Too few eligible surfaces make "scan everything" dominant (SN D.12); a decorative gauge makes a lie a non-event.
430	*Edge notes.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The one-compartment-instrument-per-room fallback is retired: the Filter's `quantity` term in `GRAPH_COMPARTMENT(cid, quantity)` (PF-9) and the Graph's published `true_value` kinds (LS-19 additions) make `inst_cryo_bay_T` eligible beside `inst_cryo_bay_p_o2`. Placement is Derelict Authoring's; the record format and the lints are this GDD's. The glyph rows carry STATE, not REMOTE: a glyph is an 8x8 mark on the module housing, so it is always local to the machine it reports (IW-6, IW-17).
431	
432	**IW-30. Binding validity and the DEAD instrument.**
433	*Rule.* If the bound node is DESTROYED, SALVAGED or ABSENT, or the ref is unresolvable, the instrument shows its **DEAD** frame: a glass hairline crack (1 px Hull Grey diagonal) and the needle snapped to a 4-px stub at a fixed angle (an honest static frame on the sheet); no prompt, no card, no gleam, no tremor, no pip. The DEAD frame is truth-graded (untagged) and cannot lie. A compartment-bound gauge is never DEAD while the compartment exists. A missing Filter datum falls back to the honest path (PF-44). *(orchestrator ruling: the art-director's snapped stub over the ux-designer's "needle at the low stop"; a needle at zero would assert "reads empty" instead of "has no reading".)*
434	*Why.* "Dead gauges on a module" are falsifier-map class C (DA); a gauge that vanishes would read as a bug, one that keeps reading would read a destroyed thing.
435	*Edge notes.* The stub is not a lie: no tag, no `lie_surface_id`.
436	
437	**IW-31. Placement record (requested) and subject registration.**
438	*Rule.* Layout and Derelict Authoring are asked for an instrument placement record (registry: `instrument_placement_record`) authored as a `Kit placement` (category `mach` or `prop`) carrying `instrument_id` (a key into `assets/data/instruments/`), `node_ref` or `room_key` plus `quantity`, `mount` WALL_FACE | MACHINE_PANEL, `host_face`, and since the design review `mount_room`, `subject_room`, `host_node` and an optional `witness_anchor_px` (the screen anchor of the drawn witness, a card keep-out, D.6); Layout's `subject_anchors(section_id)` exposes `anchor_px` so Interaction registers an `INSTRUMENT` subject. The node-to-subject binding that SN-16's lit-entry rule names as its one assumption is authored data here; the sim never queries Instruments at runtime (KRN H10). Derelict Authoring lints `INSTRUMENT_NO_BINDING`, `PANEL_GAUGE_VERB_CONFLICT` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (an INSTRUMENT on a MACHINE_PANEL that also carries an interactable verb target, an ERROR while OQ-IW-39 is open) and the at-least-3-eligible-surfaces floor. *(provisional — routed to Layout and Derelict Authoring)* (advisor ruling R23)
439	*Why.* LY-4's schema has Hardpoint, Anchor, Fixture anchor, Kit placement and Loose slot but no instrument with a Graph binding; without a record the binding lives nowhere.
440	
441	**IW-32. Sound.**
442	*Rule.* Instruments request no sound directly. A lying instrument's sound is the Filter's request (`FA_LIE_SIG_GAUGE` for needle, card (needle and numeral) and glyph; `FA_LIE_SIG_SPRITE` for housing and machine; PF-20; Audio owns assets and mix). An honest instrument's tick, settle and tremor are motion only. Card open and close sounds are UI-bus, Audio-owned, and triggered by a presentation-local `card_opened` / `card_closed` signal Instruments publish (the outbound half of registry `inspect_card_context_signal`; event names `UI_INSTRUMENT_CARD_OPEN` / `_CLOSE` requested, Audio owns the naming) *(provisional — Adaptive Audio reply owed)*. Direction-of-change agreement (AAV-17): the machine frame, the sight-glass and the lamp brightness follow the same Graph value the audio reads; a sagging hum beside a full-speed rotor frame is a contradiction the Presenter must not create unless that frame is the lie.
443	*Why.* The Filter owns lie sounds and Audio owns assets and mix (PF-20); an honest instrument that made its own sound would add a sound channel with no witness value.
444	
445	**IW-33. Pause, restore and hard start.**
446	*Rule.* Pause freezes `present_time` and with it every instrument motion (the world freezes undimmed, ART 7.4); an open card is closed by the pause itself (IW-24, a context change) and is not restored on resume *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2)*. On `hard_start` (restore, force_stage) the settle triple, tremor envelope, numeral throttle and cull history are reset: the needle shows `displayed_pm` from the first frame with no settle and no glide ramp, any open card closes, and tremor restarts from its onset ramp if the predicate still holds. A camera cut, zoom step or window resize re-projects every placement and re-chooses the card side by a cut; no settle fires. Instruments persist and replicate nothing (PIPE PR-9; PF-33).
447	*Why.* ART 7.4: the world simply stops, undimmed; a restore must reproduce what the player was shown, so no presentation state may survive it.
448	
449	**IW-34. Fallbacks and cut order.**
450	*Rule.* If the card is cut: `inspect` stays bound and dormant; stage-1 reach loses the card surface (IW-21). If the per-instance gleam transport fails (Filter spike S-1): housing and glyph gleams are cut first, never the needle or the card numeral well. If the terminal-fitting mount is rejected: dials only on MACHINE_PANEL mounts. If the art-director rejects the alarm mark: no mark (sweep and sound only). If the user declines the D96 default (card tremor, suppressed under `reduced_motion`): the held notch on the card in all modes *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The Filter's no-cache wording refresh landed on 2026-10-27 (OQ-IW-1 closed); `prev_honest_pm` and the rest, window and dwell scalars are this GDD's presentation-local scalars (IW-11, C14). Stage-3 machine-frame sets and the stage-2 lamp-housing pair are the cuttable tier (a cut removes SPRITE_SWAP eligibility through `has_both_frames`; routed to Sanity to refresh SN-16's stage-3 `KIND_W` weights if taken); the MVP floor is dial + level sight-glass + card + alarm mark + honest WORN.
451	*Why.* A solo developer's art load is the binding constraint (about 20 sheets at P0); every fallback keeps the P1 and P4 contract and removes only presentation.
452	
453	**IW-35. Flagged, not edited.**
454	*Rule.* Missing index edges (Pipeline PIPE:302, Emitter State EM:339, Failure & Trail soft pair, Sanity lie targets) and the unowned module-presenter row are recorded in Dependencies (K-10, K-11, advisor ruling R26); the stale ART 7.0 / 2.5 pod-dash lines are the art-director's (WM:1187). This GDD edits neither the index, the art bible nor another GDD. The field-check / scanner reading is HUD & Suit Layer's to draw (a hand-tool reading on the hand rail and an honest anchor at MVP, SN-19); Instruments supply only the shared honest-digit mechanism of IW-14 as a reusable component (advisor ruling R15; K-9; refresh owed on BS:1206).
455	*Why.* The index's explicit edges and the neighbours' own rows must not be silently rewritten by a downstream author (producer owns the index; art-director owns the bible).
456	
457	**IW-36. Legibility contract: every figure at every rung.**
458	*Rule.* Every legibility figure in this GDD is stated at **every** zoom rung `k` in [1, `k_auto` + 2] (720p and Steam Deck 1280x800 `k_auto` 2: 1..4; 1080p 3: 1..5; 1440p 4: 1..6; 2160p 6: 1..8) and at HUD scale `H` from `H_default` = max(`k_auto`, 3) (Pipeline registry formula `hud_multiplier`, `H_default = max(k, 3)`; `k` there is the default rung `k_auto`, because the HUD does not change with zoom, PIPE PR-12) to 2 x `H_default` (`HUD_MIN_SCALE` 3), including the Steam Deck case (`H` 3 over `k` 2), the largest field (zoom 1x at 2160p) and the maximum `H` on small displays; the table is D.7. By construction the needle stroke (2 art px) is at least 2 screen px at every rung; the gleam and tremor art-px size is raised only at `k` 1 (D.5, D.9); the world needle's absolute floor is `NEEDLE_SCREEN_MIN_PX` (`[PLACEHOLDER]` 24, accessibility tier): DIAL_S at `k` 1 (18 screen px) is below it and is accepted because `k` 1 is a deliberate zoom-out and the card is the precision path; at zoom 1x on 2160p the world dial is a 56-px arc in a 3840-px frame, readable only by pattern and needle, which is the design's weakest point and is carried as a risk, not hidden. Tremor's marginal visibility at `k` 1 on the largest field is acceptable only because instrument tremor is never the only tell: every IW-12 stress source also has a sound or world-witness tell owned by Adaptive Audio or Failure & Trail, so zooming out never removes the warning (IW-12; AC-IW-106).
459	*Why.* Reflexion-log rule: an invariant written against the default must be re-checked whenever a later decision adds reachable states (zoom steps, resolutions).
460	
461	**IW-37. Strings and localisation.**
462	*Rule.* Every string on an instrument or card is a `tr()` StringName key: the label (`name_key`), the unit (`unit_key`) and nothing else; a world gauge carries no text. Labels are never truncated (truncation would make two instruments ambiguous): a label wider than the plate's text width (plate width minus 8 art px) wraps to a second row and the plate grows by 7 art px, and the placement cap is recomputed with the taller plate (D.6). The bitmap instrument face covers the shipped Latin set; scripts it lacks (CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic right-to-left) need a fallback face, and the vector reading face is barred on instruments by ART 7.1 (OQ-IW-14). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **The card degrades element by element and is never removed for a locale:** the numeral cells (Latin digits with the slashed zero) and the dial or glass render in every locale, and a `name_key` or `unit_key` containing a glyph the bitmap face lacks falls back, for that one element, to the default-locale (Latin) string and then to the instrument's part-number stencil (`instrument_id`), so the only precision path survives everywhere. The decimal mark follows the locale key and is part of the plate variant. No string says a state, a verdict or a lie (IA-39; PF-38).
463	*Why.* A label that can be mistranslated into a verdict is a P4 oracle; a truncated label makes two instruments ambiguous and breaks the second-opinion check.
464	
465	**IW-38. Diagnostics: a dev-only probe and nothing else.**
466	*Rule.* In development builds only, each instrument exposes a read-only `drawn_value(ref)` (the value it actually drew this frame, answering the Debug Overlay's render-probe ask DO-22, whose `DEFECT_BYPASS` class detects a corruptible node that skipped the Filter) and an `instrument_diag(ref)` record `{instrument_id, ref_key, motion_mode as drawn, settle_active, tremor_active, card_open, state}`. Both are tagged dev-only and stripped from release builds; neither is a value source for any gameplay or presentation node; neither exposes `true_value` (the Overlay calls that itself, DIAGNOSTIC). Instruments publish a stable integer `ref_key` per instrument (the Filter's, PF-9) and keep four counters for the Overlay and the lints: `diag.instr_pm_clamped` (a `displayed_pm` outside 0..1000 was clamped), `diag.inspect_unresolved` (IW-24), `diag.instr_quantity_collision` and `diag.gleam_over_cap` (IW-16). The Overlay treats an absent probe as `bypass_check: ABSENT`, never clean (DO-22). In development builds only, Instruments registers one diagnostics channel at composition-root time under the Debug Overlay's channel contract (DO-12, `diag_panel_contract`), carrying the counters `diag.instr_pm_clamped`, `diag.inspect_unresolved`, `diag.instr_quantity_collision` and `diag.gleam_over_cap` and the `instrument_diag(ref)` rows. The channel is a dev-only panel registration, not a kernel block, hook, mutator or dirty key, so IW-2's zero-registration rule is unchanged; it is stripped from release builds.
467	*Why.* The Overlay's classifier can otherwise only compare `perceived` with `true_value`; a node that bypasses the Filter is invisible to it.
468	*Edge notes.* An out-of-range `displayed_pm` is clamped to the end stop and counted; it is never an error shown to the player.

470	### States and Transitions
471	
472	An instrument has three independent axes: a **visibility axis** (does the world's light reach it, is its card open, does its binding still exist), a **motion axis** driven by the Filter's `motion_mode`, and an **ALARM flag**. All state is presentation-local, non-persistent and non-replicated; none of it is a sim block, and every state is reset by `hard_start` (IW-33). The sim never reads any of it.
473	
474	#### S1. Visibility axis
475	
476	| State | Meaning | Visual | Prompt / card | Entry | Exit | Who may cause it |
477	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
478	| `DARK` | exists; `lit(ref)` false | the renderer shows a dark or dim face (HullSurface lighting, not an Instruments hide); the gleam rides the host and is dark too; the pip, if the loop runs, is visible | prompt hidden; card refused | scene load with no light on the face; `lit` falls below `LIT_OFF_PM` 120 | `lit` rises to `LIT_ON_PM` 150 | Emitter State (the `lit` bit, owned by the technical-artist); Lighting (what the beam, fixtures, lantern pools and Chemlight reach); the player (aim, movement, throwing a glowstick) |
479	| `LIT` | `lit(ref)` true | readable face; honest or perceived reading; gleam if lying | prompt may show (focus plus debounce); card openable | `lit` rises; a card closes while the instrument is still lit | `lit` falls; binding lost; card opens | Emitter State; Interaction (focus, prompt); the player |
480	| `CARD_OPEN` | `LIT` and the Adapter context is `inspect_card` for this ref | the wall gauge unchanged, plus the card on layer 2 | card open | `inspect` pressed on a lit target (the primary focus or the secondary INSTRUMENT slot, IW-21); no debounce gates the press *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | any IW-24 close condition | the Adapter (`{inspect_card, ref}` signal) for entry and for `inspect` / `cancel` / B exits; Emitter State (`lit` false); Graph (binding lost); Save/Load via kernel restore; Pipeline (camera cut re-places, never closes) |
481	| `DEAD` | bound node DESTROYED, SALVAGED or ABSENT, or the ref is unresolvable | DEAD frame: hairline crack, snapped needle stub | prompt hidden; card refused | binding lost | binding restored (section re-load) | Graph (`node(id).state`, section load and unload); Layout (placement) |
482	
483	#### S2. Motion axis (inside `DARK`, `LIT`, `CARD_OPEN`; independent of visibility)
484	
485	*(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* `REST`, `SETTLING` and `FILTER_DRIVEN` are mutually exclusive states. **Tremor is an orthogonal flag, as ALARM is in S3**: it can be set in `REST` or `SETTLING` (never in `FILTER_DRIVEN`) and it adds its offset to whatever base the state draws (E-IW-10, AC-IW-65), so a settle and a tremor are active together by construction.
486	
487	| State | Meaning | Entry | Exit | Who may cause it |
488	|---|---|---|---|---|
489	| `REST` | **at rest in time (IW-11 (b))**: no honest sample for `INSTR_REST_STEPS` Graph steps and no settle active; the needle sits on one pixel *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | initial; `INSTR_REST_STEPS` steps after the last honest sample once any ramp or settle has ended; on `hard_start`; on return to HONEST (the tremor flag does not affect `REST`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | the first honest sample (a ramp, or a settle if it passes the jump test); non-HONEST mode | (resting state) |
490	| `SETTLING` | closed-form settle in progress (IW-11) | a jump from rest while HONEST | `INSTR_SETTLE_MS` elapsed (to `REST`); re-based by another change (stays `SETTLING` with a fresh triple); non-HONEST mode (cleared at once) | the Graph (a real discrete change of the honest displayed value); the Filter (`motion_mode`) |
491	| `TREMOR` flag (orthogonal to `REST` and `SETTLING`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | honest stress tremor (IW-12) | predicate true while HONEST (onset ramp `TREMOR_ONSET_MS`) | predicate false (decay `TREMOR_DECAY_MS`, then the flag clears and the base state is unchanged); non-HONEST mode (cleared at once) | the Graph (the stress predicate from `read_view`: hazard-mode descriptors via `failures(filter)` (including an OVERLOAD descriptor on a cable of the bound loop component), and `stress_active` if granted); never Attention, sanity or a timer |
492	| `FILTER_DRIVEN` | `motion_mode` is GLIDE, TICK, STALE or RETURN; Instruments draw the received `displayed_pm` verbatim on the needle or meniscus (the Filter's trajectory, wander included, which never rests) and, on the card, the received digits (continuous tick, or the held digits of STALE) | the Filter's `motion_mode` leaves HONEST (the settle triple, tremor and notch are cleared that frame) | `motion_mode` returns to HONEST (CLEAR; discrepancy under `LEAK_EPS_DEG`, PF-12): to `REST`, no event, no flash | the Perception Filter only; Instruments never infer it |
493	
494	Reduced motion changes only how `SETTLING` and the `TREMOR` flag are drawn (a step and a held notch pair, IW-27); the states and their causes are the same.
495	
496	#### S3. ALARM flag
497	
498	`ALARM` is set while an `alarm_eligible` `FailureDescriptor` exists on the bound subject (read through `failures(filter)`, refreshed per Graph step) and cleared with it. It is orthogonal to every state above and to `motion_mode`: a lying needle never sets, moves or clears it. Only the Graph causes it (LS-13 fairness gate). It is drawn only on housings that carry the mark (IW-19) and never on the card.
499	
500	#### S4. Transitions
501	
502	| From | Event / guard | To | Notes |
503	|---|---|---|---|
504	| `DARK` | `lit(ref)` true | `LIT` | no dwell (EM-22) |
505	| `LIT` | `lit(ref)` false | `DARK` | an open card closes in the same render frame |
506	| `LIT` | `inspect` on a lit target (primary focus or secondary slot); no debounce gates the press *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | `CARD_OPEN` | the Adapter publishes `{inspect_card, ref}`; no command is submitted |
507	| `CARD_OPEN` | `inspect` again, or `cancel` (X) / B | `LIT` | |
508	| `CARD_OPEN` | `lit(ref)` false, reach lost, section transit, restore or `hard_start` | `DARK` / `LIT` per cause | immediate close; re-open needs a new press |
509	| `CARD_OPEN` | the Adapter context becomes `chart_table` (pause) or `chat`, or `loco_state` becomes STAGGERED, DOWNED, DEAD or IN_POD *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | `LIT` or `DARK` per `lit` | closes in the same render frame; not re-opened when the context returns to `gameplay` (E-IW-60); in co-op the overlay does not pause the sim, so the card never stays drawn under a modal |
510	| `CARD_OPEN` | movement intent past the dead-zone *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | `LIT` or `DARK` per `lit` | closes and the avatar moves in the same frame (IW-25, E-IW-29) |
511	| `CARD_OPEN` | binding lost | `DEAD` | card closes that frame |
512	| any | binding lost (node DESTROYED, SALVAGED or ABSENT; ref unresolvable) | `DEAD` | |
513	| `DEAD` | binding restored | `DARK` or `LIT` per `lit` | section re-load |
514	| `REST` | first honest sample whose accumulated change passes the jump test inside the window (IW-11 (b)) on a `settle_eligible` quantity *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | `SETTLING` | triple set *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
515	| `SETTLING` | any further change of the honest displayed value | `SETTLING` | re-based: `from` = value now drawn |
516	| any HONEST state (`REST` or `SETTLING`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | stress predicate true while HONEST | `TREMOR` flag set; the base state is unchanged | onset ramp; the drawn position is the base plus the tremor offset, clamped (E-IW-10) |
517	| `TREMOR` flag set | predicate false | flag cleared after the decay; base state unchanged | decay, then the needle rests on a pixel |
518	| any HONEST state | `motion_mode` becomes GLIDE, TICK, STALE or RETURN | `FILTER_DRIVEN` | triple, tremor and notch cleared that frame |
519	| `FILTER_DRIVEN` | `motion_mode` HONEST | `REST` | no settle (E-IW-36: a return is not a jump) |
520	| any | `hard_start`, cull re-entry, camera cut | `REST` | all presentation scalars reset; the needle shows `displayed_pm` at once |
521	| any | pause (kernel PAUSED) | unchanged, frozen | `present_time` stops; an open card was already closed by the `chart_table` row above and stays closed on resume; the plate does not animate back in *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2)* |
522	
523	**Invariants.** (I-1) `CARD_OPEN` implies `LIT` at the moment of the frame in which it is drawn. (I-2) `SETTLING` and the `TREMOR` flag imply `motion_mode` HONEST in that frame *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. (I-3) `DEAD` implies no prompt, no card, no gleam, no tremor, no pip. (I-4) At most one card is open per client, and it is for the ref of the target of the press, the primary focus when it is an INSTRUMENT and otherwise the secondary INSTRUMENT slot (IW-21), at the time of the press *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
524	
525	### Interactions with Other Systems
526	
527	"In" is what Instruments take; "Out" is what Instruments give. **Instruments give nothing to the simulation**: no command, no mutator, no hook, no block, no dirty key, no persisted field. Status vocabulary: **designed** (a GDD on disk, header Status Designed); **designed in this run** (written in this orchestrated run, may be revised); **undesigned-provisional** (no GDD on disk; this GDD states a request and re-checks it when the neighbour lands). Glob of `design/gdd/` at authoring: 27 files including this one (re-counted 2026-10-27: 28 `.md` files, the 26 MVP GDDs plus `game-concept.md` and `systems-index.md`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; HUD & Suit Layer and Debug Overlay (True Values) are Status Designed (**designed in this run**); Accessibility Settings does not exist.
528	
529	#### I-A. Upstream systems (Instruments depend on them)
530	
531	| Neighbour (status) | In (to Instruments) | Out (from Instruments) | Interface owner | Named interface |

589	## Formulas
590	
591	Every formula below is presentation-side. None is hashed, persisted or replicated, none is read by another system's simulation, and none feeds the kernel's `state_hash` (KRN D.12); so floating-point arithmetic on `present_time` is permitted for motion (D.1, D.4, D.5), while every quantity read from the Graph or the Filter stays an integer (per-mille, dkPa, mC, permille) and every formatted string is integer-only (D.3). D.2 and D.12 run in the instrument build tool, not in the game. The Perception Filter's formulas (glide parameters, PF D.2; `lie_displayed_value`, PF D.3; wander, PF D.4; `lying_digit_tick_schedule`, PF D.9; fringe width, PF D.10; presentation hash, PF D.14) and the Graph's `atmosphere_derive` (LSG D.3) are **cited by registry name and never restated**; a number quoted from one of them carries its owner. D.1 to D.12 are registered as formulas, not only as constants, so that both bounds of each travel together (reflexion log: "when a formula has two bounds, register the formula"); registry entries are written from this final text, not from the specialist drafts. `INSTR_`-prefixed constants are this GDD's `[PLACEHOLDER]` values (Tuning Knobs); `[UNV]` marks an engine behaviour with no reference file (the engine reference has no `scripting.md` and no `core.md`). **Rounding convention (one rule for every formula):** `round` in D.1 (`tip`), D.5 (`o`) and D.11 (`y(pm)`) is half away from zero (the behaviour of GDScript `round`, so `round(0.5)` = 1 and `round(-0.5)` = -1); `floor` is the mathematical floor; `floor_div` is the explicit helper of D.3 (never native integer division on a negative numerator); per-mille, dkPa and mC values are integers, so a "16.7 pm" quantum is the integer step 16 or 17 depending on where the value falls on the span. Every acceptance vector in this document uses this convention.

592	
593	### D.1 Needle angle, honest sample ramp and tip pixel (`needle_angle`)
594	
595	The needle angle formula is defined as:
596	
597	`a = clamp( ((T_c - t_sample) + tick_alpha) / GRAPH_STEP_TICKS, 0, 1 )`
598	
599	`pm_honest = prev_honest_pm + (target_pm - prev_honest_pm) * a`
600	
601	`pm_draw = pm_honest` (HONEST, no settle) `| settle_response(from_pm, to_pm, t_jump)` (HONEST, a jump, D.4) `| displayed_pm` (every other `motion_mode`, verbatim)
602	
603	`theta(pm) = -arc_deg / 2 + pm * arc_deg / 1000` (degrees, clockwise from 12 o'clock)
604	
605	`tip(pm) = round( pivot + needle_len_px * (sin theta, -cos theta) )` (whole art px, y down)
606	
607	`px_per_pm = needle_len_px * (arc_deg * pi / 180) / 1000`; `tip_speed = needle_len_px * omega` (px/s)
608	
609	**Variables:**
610	
611	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
612	|---|---|---|---|---|
613	| `T_c` | int ticks | >= 0 | kernel tick of this render frame (read view) | the tick the frame is drawn at |
614	| `t_sample` | int ticks | <= `T_c` | local | the tick at which the current honest sample was first drawn (the Filter's honest memo was invalidated by an LS-20 quantum crossing) |
615	| `tick_alpha` | float | [0, 1] | PIPE PR-8 rule 5 (kernel `tick_alpha`, clamped) | the one interpolation factor between kernel ticks |
616	| `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` | int | 6 (REG) | Graph | one Graph step is 100 ms |
617	| `displayed_pm` | int per mille | 0..1000 (out of range is clamped and counted, `diag.instr_pm_clamped`) | `Perceived` (PF-8) | the Filter's displayed reading |

706	### D.4 Closed-form settle (`settle_response`)
707	
708	The settle response formula is defined as:
709	
710	`tau = present_time - t_jump`
711	
712	`y(tau) = 1 - exp(-zeta * omega * tau) * ( cos(omega_d * tau) + (zeta / sqrt(1 - zeta^2)) * sin(omega_d * tau) )`, `omega_d = omega * sqrt(1 - zeta^2)`
713	
714	`drawn_pm = clamp( from_pm + (to_pm - from_pm) * y(tau), 0, 1000 )` for `0 <= tau < INSTR_SETTLE_MS / 1000`; `drawn_pm = to_pm` afterwards
715	
716	**Trigger** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: rest is defined in time, IW-11 (b))*: with `rest_pm` the value the needle held when the instrument left rest, a new honest sample starts a settle iff `motion_mode` is HONEST, **the quantity's calibration record has `settle_eligible` true** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (true for `load` only at MVP; every other quantity draws the D.1 ramp whatever its rate, so a fast vent or a hatch to vacuum on `p_o2` or `P`, which can exceed 40 pm in 400 ms above about 30 dkPa/s, is a sweep and never a settle: detent, not settle), the instrument was at rest (no honest sample for `INSTR_REST_STEPS` Graph steps and no settle active) when the window opened, the sample arrives within `INSTR_SETTLE_WINDOW_STEPS` Graph steps of the first sample after rest, and `abs(target_pm - rest_pm) >= INSTR_SETTLE_JUMP_PM`; then `from_pm := the value now drawn`, `to_pm := target_pm`, `t_jump := present_time`. A sample that does not satisfy the test is drawn by the D.1 ramp, and a run that leaves its window without a jump is a sweep until rest is re-entered. **Re-base:** while a settle is active, any further change of the honest displayed value sets `from_pm := the value currently drawn`, `to_pm := the new value`, `t_jump := now` (velocity is discarded); one triple always suffices. Any non-HONEST frame clears the triple and bypasses this formula.
